14- That the comparison occurs between two bringings out, that is: your Lord's bringing you out of your house — which is Mecca — while you disliked your going out, and the outcome of that was good, victory and triumph, is like your Lord's bringing you out of Medina while some of the believers disliked it, which will be followed by that victory and triumph.
15- The kāf is for comparison by way of figurative speech, like the saying of someone to his servant: "As I sent you to my enemies and they considered you weak, and you asked for reinforcement and I reinforced you and strengthened you, take them now and punish them thus; and as I clothed you and provided for you, do such and such; and as I did good to you, thank me for it."
It is clear that the outcome of these aspects is one, so ponder, and Allah protect you.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational similes (tashbīhāt tamthīliyya) occurring in the verses we have pointed out during the parsing, because of their close connection with it.
2- Generality and particularity in His saying «ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل» after His saying «يريد الله أن يحق الحق بكلماته». The precise distinction between the two statements is that in the first the will is mentioned as unrestricted, not bound to the particular event, as though it were said: "You wish that the one without might be yours, and it is Allah's way, Exalted is He, to will the establishment of the truth and the eradication of unbelief in general; and because He willed to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, He gave you the one with might." So between the two statements there are generality and particularity, and unrestrictedness and restriction, and it is not hidden how much emphasis there is in this for the meaning, by mentioning it in two ways: unrestrictedly and restrictedly.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ﴾: on the day of Badr the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the people, saying: "شاهت الوجوه" ("May the faces be disfigured"), that is, may they be made ugly; and that too was a cause of their rout.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾, and also (موَهِّن). If you wish you put it in iḍāfa (genitive construct), and if you wish you give it tanwīn (nunation) and put [the following noun] in the accusative. Like it are (إنّ اللّهَ بَالِغُ أمْرِهِ، وبَالغٌ أمْرَهُ) and (كاشفاتُ ضُرِّه، وكاشِفَاتٌ ضُرَّه).

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾: Abū Jahl said on that day: "O Allah, give victory to the better of the two religions and the one more deserving of victory." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾, meaning victory.
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: he said: putting a kasra on its alif (i.e. reading إِنَّ) is dearer to me than putting a fatḥa on it, because in the reading of ʿAbdallāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (وإن الله لمع المؤمنين), and this makes the kasra good, as the beginning of a new sentence. Whoever gives it a fatḥa connects it with ﴿وَلَن تُغْنِيَ عَنْكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ﴾, meaning: "because of its great number and because Allah is with the believers"; so its position is accusative (naṣb), since the genitive (khafḍ) [i.e. an implied preposition] is suitable in it.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتْنَةً لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ﴾: He commanded them and then forbade them, and there is in it a touch of the jazāʾ (conditional apodosis), even though it is a prohibition. Like it is His saying ﴿يأيها النمل ادخلوا مساكِنكم لا يحطِمنَّكم﴾: she commanded them and then forbade them, and there is in it the sense of the jazāʾ.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُوۤاْ إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ﴾ was revealed about the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn) specifically.
His saying: ﴿فَآوَاكُمْ﴾ means: to Medina; ﴿وَأَيَّدَكُم بِنَصْرِهِ﴾ means: He strengthened you.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَخُونُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ وَتَخُونُوۤاْ أَمَانَاتِكُمْ﴾: if you wish you make it jussive (jazm) as a prohibition, and if you wish you make it ṣarf (the "turning-away" construction) and put it in the accusative. [The poet] said:
لا تنه عن خُلُقٍ وتأتِىَ مِثلَه * عار عليك إِذا فعلت عظيم
(Do not forbid a trait while you yourself do its like; a great shame upon you if you do.)
And in one of the two readings it is (ولا تخونوا أماناتِكم), so here too it may be jussive or accusative.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿إَن تَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّكُمْ فُرْقَاناً﴾: He says: an opening (victory) and help. Likewise His saying ﴿يوم الفرقانِ يوم التقى الجمعانِ﴾: the day of the opening and of victory.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾: a group of Quraysh gathered and said: "What is your view about Muḥammad ﷺ?" Iblīs came in among them in the form of a man from the people of Najd. ʿAmr ibn Hishām said: "My view is that you confine him in a house, plaster it up over him, open a small window for him and press hard on him until he dies." Iblīs rejected that and said: "What a bad opinion your opinion is!" Abū al-Bakhtarī ibn Hishām said: "My view is that he be put on a camel and then driven off with it until he perishes, or some of the Arabs rid you of him." Iblīs said: "What a bad opinion! Would you send away from yourselves a man who has corrupted most of you, so that he falls in with others than you? Perhaps he would then raid you with them." The wicked one, Abū Jahl, said: "My view is that we go to him with a man from every clan of Quraysh and strike him with our swords." Iblīs said: "The right opinion is what this young man has given." Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ with the news, and he left Mecca, he and Abū Bakr. So His saying (ليثبتوك) means: to confine you in the house; (أو يخرِجوك): on the camel; (أو يقتلوك).
[Translator's note: the source writes «صى الله عليه وسلم», evidently a misprint for «صلى الله عليه وسلم»; rendered as ﷺ.]

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ ٱللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَـٰذَا هُوَ ٱلْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ﴾: in (الحق) there is the accusative and the nominative. If you make (هو) a noun [i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject)], you put الحق in the nominative by هو. If you make it an ʿimād (support pronoun; the Kufan term for the separating pronoun), functioning like a ṣila (redundant link), you put الحق in the accusative. Do the same with the sisters of kāna, and with aẓunnu (I think) and its sisters, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿ويرى الذِين أوتو العِلم الذى أنزِل إليك مِن ربك هو الحق﴾: you put الحق in the accusative because (رأيت) is one of the sisters of ẓanantu. Every place where yafʿalu or faʿala would be suitable in place of the accusative "fiʿl" [i.e. the predicate] admits the ʿimād and the accusative of that "fiʿl"; and it also admits its nominative by هو, if you make it a noun. And the alif and lām (the definite article) are indispensable when you find a way to them. So if you say: وجدت عبدالله هو خيرا منك وشرا منك أو أفضل منك ("I found ʿAbdallāh better than you / worse than you / more excellent than you"), then in whatever resembles this "fiʿl" there is both accusative and nominative: the accusative on the basis that the alif and lām are intended, even if they cannot be inserted; and the nominative on the basis that you make (هو) a noun. So you say: ظننت أخاك هو أصغُر منك and هو أصغرَ منك ("I thought your brother younger than you").
When you come to proper nouns such as ʿAmr and Muḥammad, or to nouns in iḍāfa such as أبيك (your father) and أخيك (your brother), you put them in the nominative, saying: أظنّ زيدا هو أخوك and أظنّ أخاك هو زيد, putting it in the nominative, since you have not brought the sign of the "returned" element (al-mardūd) but have brought هو, which is the sign of the noun. The sign of the "returned" element is that every "fiʿl" which has no alif and lām is brought back with alif and lām and refers back to the noun; so (هو) is a support for the noun and (the alif and lām) a support for the "fiʿl". Since the alif and lām could not be supplied, and it was not proper to intend them in زيد, because it is a [proper] name, nor in الأخ, because it is in iḍāfa, they preferred the nominative. It is proper in (أفضل منك) because you drop (من) and say: رأيتك أنت الأفضل ("I saw you to be the most excellent"); but it is not proper in (زيد) or in (الأخ) to intend an alif and lām. Al-Kisāʾī used to allow it, saying: رأيت أخاك هو زيدا and رأيت زيدا هو أخاك. And it is permissible, just as it was permissible in (أفضل) because of the intention, the intention of the alif and lām; and likewise it was permissible in زيد and أخيك. When the alif and lām are possible for you and yet you do not bring them, use the nominative; so you say: رأيت زيدا هو قائم and رأيت عمرا هو جالس.
The poet said:
إجِدَّك لن تزال نجِىَّ هَمّ * تبيت الليل أنت له ضجيع
(Is it in earnest that you will never cease to be the confidant of care, spending the night as its bedfellow?)
And the accusative is permissible in (ليت) by way of the ʿimād, and the nominative for one who says: ليتك قائما. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
ليت الشباب هو الرجيع على الفتى * والشيب كان هو البدئُ الأوّل
(Would that youth were what returns to a young man, and grey hair were the first beginning.)
He used the accusative with (ليت) by way of the ʿimād and the nominative with كان by way of the noun. Definite and indefinite are the same in this.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾: (أَنَّ) came both at its beginning and its end because it is a jazāʾ (conditional), like His saying ﴿كُتِبَ عليه أَنه مَنْ تَولاَّهُ فأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّه﴾ and like His saying ﴿أَلم يَعْلَمُوا أَنه مَنْ يحادِدِ اللَّه ورسولَه فأَنَّ له نارَ جهنَّم﴾. It is permissible in the second (أنّ) to give its alif a kasra, because its dropping is permissible: do you not see that if you said (اعلموا أنّ ما غنمتم من شىء فللّه خمسه) it would be sound? So since its dropping is sound, one gives it a kasra.
His saying: ﴿وَلِذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾: the kinsfolk of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾: the orphans and the poor of the people [at large]; the orphans and the poor of Banū Hāshim are not included in it.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَنتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: al-ʿudwa is the bank of the valley; (الدينا) [i.e. الدنيا, "the nearer"] is the side next to Medina, and (القصوى) ("the farther") the side next to Mecca.
[Translator's note: the source prints «الدينا», apparently a misprint for «الدنيا».]
His saying ﴿وَٱلرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ means Abū Sufyān and the caravan; they were on the seashore.
His saying ﴿أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ is accusative; it means: a place lower than you. Had He described them as being low, meaning "and the caravan were lower", it would have been permissible, in the nominative.
His saying: ﴿وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَيَّ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ﴾: it is written with idghām (assimilation), with a single yāʾ, and that is the reading of most of the readers. Some of them read (حَيىَِ عن بيّنة) with the two made distinct. They assimilated the yāʾ into the yāʾ, though they ought not to have done so, because the second yāʾ is bound to take the fatḥa in faʿala; they assimilated because two vowelled letters of the same kind met. Assimilation is permissible in the dual because of the fixed vowel of the last yāʾ, so you say of two men: قد حَيّا and حَيِيا. In the plural one ought not to assimilate, because its yāʾ would receive the ḍamma while what precedes it has a kasra, so it ought to become quiescent and drop before the wāw of the plural. Yet sometimes the Arabs have used assimilation in the plural, aiming at making the verb forms uniform and having them all doubled.
So they said for حَيِيت: حَيُّوا, and for عيِيت: عَيُّوا. One of them recited to me:
يَحِدن بِنا عن كلّ حَىٍّ كأننا * أخاريس عَيُّوا بالسلام وبالنَّسْبِ
(They [the camels] veer with us away from every tribe, as though we were mutes who could manage neither greeting nor lineage.)
He means النّسَب. Another said:
مِن الذين إذا قلنا: حَدِيثَكم * عَيُّوا، وإن نحن حَدَّثناهُمُ شَغِبَوا
(Of those who, when we say "Your story!", are tongue-tied, and when we talk to them, make an uproar.)
The Arabs are agreed on assimilating التحيّة and التحيّات because of the vowel of the last yāʾ in them, just as they favoured assimilating عىَّ and حَىَّ because of the fixed vowel in them. It may also be correct to assimilate yāʾ into yāʾ in يَحْيا and يَعْيا, though this is rarer than the assimilation in حىّ, because the yāʾ of يحيا is quiescent when it is in the nominative position, so the vowel in it is not fixed. Its justification is that when you put it in the accusative, as in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, ﴿أَليس ذلِك بِقادِرٍ على أَن يُحْيِىَ المَوْتَى﴾, assimilation is correct there; then you make the speech uniform, so that it has assimilation in the nominative and the jussive too; and you say (هو يُحِىُّ ويُمِيت). One of them recited to me:
وكأنها بين النساءِ سبِيكةٌ * تمشى بِسُدَّةِ بَيْتها فَتُعِىُّ
(As if she, among the women, were an ingot [of gold]; she walks to the threshold of her house and grows weary.)
And likewise يَحَيَّان and يَحَيُّون.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَقَالَ لاَ غَالِبَ لَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ﴾: this is Iblīs, who appeared in the form of a man of Banū Kināna called Surāqa ibn Juʿshum. Al-Farrāʾ said: His saying ﴿وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ﴾ means: [your protector] against my people, Banū Kināna, so that they do not interfere with you, and so that they will be with you against Muḥammad ﷺ. When he saw the angels he recognised them, so "he turned back on his heels" (نَكَصَ على عَقِبَيْه). Al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām said to him: "O Surāqa, fleeing without a fight?!" He said: (إنى أَرَى ما لا تَرَوْن) ("I see what you do not see").

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ وَذُوقُواْ﴾ means: "and they say", implied (muḍmar), as He said: ﴿ولَوْ تَرَى إذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهم عِنْدَ رَبِّهِم رَبَّنَا﴾, meaning: they say: (رَبَّنا). And in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: ﴿وَإِذْ يرفع إِبراهِيمُ القواعِدَ من البيتِ وإِسماعيلُ﴾ "the two of them saying" ﴿رَبَّنا﴾.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ﴾: (أَنّ) is in the position of the accusative if you make (ذلك) accusative and mean: We did ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ and because ﴿أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾. If you wish, you make (ذلك) in the position of the nominative, and then you make (أنْ) in the position of the nominative, as you say: هذا ذاك ("this is that").

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ means: these denied just as the family of Pharaoh denied, so there befell them what befell the family of Pharaoh.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِم مَّنْ خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ means: if you take them captive, O Muḥammad, then make an example of them to those behind them, those whom you fear will break the covenant: ﴿فَشرِّدْ بِهِمْ﴾.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾: so that they do not break the covenant. It has sometimes been read (مِن خَلْفِهِم), with a kasra on (مِن), but it has no meaning that I approve of in view of the exegesis.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍ خِيَانَةً﴾: He says: breaking of a covenant; ﴿فَٱنْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ with the breaking [i.e. throw back the treaty to them], ﴿عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾: He says: do as they do, equally. It is also said about His saying ﴿عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾: openly, not in secret. His saying ﴿تَخافَنّ﴾ is in the position of the jussive. The Arabs hardly ever put the heavy or the light nūn [of emphasis] in a jazāʾ (conditional) until they join it to (ما); and when they join it, they prefer the nūn. That is because they found that (إمّا), when it is conditional, resembles the (إمّا) of choice ("either… or"), so they introduced the nūn so that the difference between the two might be known by it. Then they made most of its apodoses with fāʾ; thus the Revelation came. He said: ﴿فَإمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِى الحربِ فشَرِّد﴾, and ﴿فإمّا نُرِيَنَّك بعض الذِى نَعِدهم﴾, then He said ﴿فإلينا يرجعون﴾. The fāʾ was chosen because when they put the nūn with (إمّا) they make it the head of the sentence and hardly ever postpone it. It is not their usage to say: اضربه إمّا يقومَنَّ ("Hit him if he stands up"); their usage is to put it first. Since it was bound to come first, it became like something outside the condition, so they favoured the fāʾ with it and preferred it, just as they favoured it in their saying أمّا أخوكم فقاعد ("As for your brother, he is sitting"), since it resembles that.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «فاسحبوا», apparently a misprint for «فاستحبّوا» ("they favoured"); translated in that sense.]

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَبَقُوۤاْ إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ﴾ is with tāʾ (تحسبنّ), there being no disagreement about it. But Ḥamza read it with yāʾ; and we think he took it in light of the reading of ʿAbdallāh.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا إنهم لا يُعْجِزون). If (أنّهم) is not in it, it is not right for the verb of thinking (ẓann) not to fall on anything [as its object]. Had he meant: "Let not those who disbelieve think that they cannot be frustrated", it would be right, making لا a ṣila (redundant), as in His saying: ﴿وحَرامٌ على قَرْيةٍ أَهلكناها أَنّهم لا يَرْجِعون﴾, meaning: that they will return. And if (أنْ) were with (سبقوا) it would be right, so that you say (ولا يحسب الذين كفروا أن سبقوا).
If someone says: "Is it not Arab usage to say عسيت أذهب ('maybe I shall go') and أريد أقوم معك ('I want to stand with you'), with (أنْ) implied in both? So why is it not permissible to say أظن أقوم ('I think I shall stand') and أظن قمت ('I think I stood')?" I reply: if that were done with ẓanantu when the verb belongs to the one mentioned [i.e. the subject], I would allow it, even if it is a noun, as in their saying: عسى الغُوَيْرُ أَبْؤُساً ("perhaps the little cave holds misfortunes"), the proper form being with أنْ. If you say that, you would say it with aẓunnu too, saying أظن أقوم and أظن قمت, because the verb is yours. But it is not permissible to say أظن يقوم زيد, nor عسيت يقوم زيد, nor أردت يقوم زيد. It is permissible when the verb belongs to him [the subject] because, when you turn yafʿalu into fāʿil (the active participle), it is joined to it and is accusative by its owner; so one says أريد قائما ("I want [to be] standing"), the standing being yours. You do not say أريد قائما زيد; and whoever says this says the like with ẓanantu. One of them recited to me, by Dhū al-Rumma:
أَظَنَّ ابْنُ طُرْثوثِ عُتَيْبةُ ذاهبا * بعادِيَّتِى تَكْذابُه وَجعائِلُهْ
(Did Ibn Ṭurthūth, ʿUtayba, think his lying and his bribes would make off with my wronging?)
So this is a line of reasoning for the reading of Ḥamza: he makes (سبقوا) in the position of the accusative: "Let not those who disbelieve think [themselves] outstripping (sābiqīn)." But I do not like it, because it is anomalous.
[Translator's note: the opening statement that the tāʾ reading has "no disagreement" and then that Ḥamza read with yāʾ is translated as written; it seems to mean that the tāʾ reading is the agreed reading of the majority. The poetic gloss is tentative.]

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُمْ مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ﴾ means the mares. Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to us, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Strength (al-quwwa) is shooting."
His saying: ﴿تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدْوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَآخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ﴾: if you made it [وآخرين] accusative from His saying "and prepare for them, and for others besides them", it would be correct, as in His saying: ﴿والظالمين أَعَدَّ لهم عذابا أليما﴾. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: (ترهبون به عَدُوّاً لِلّهِ وعدوّكم), just as some read in [Sūrat] al-Ṣaff (كونوا أَنْصاراً لِلّهِ).

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن جَنَحُواْ لِلسَّلْمِ فَٱجْنَحْ لَهَا...﴾: if you wish you make (لها) a pronoun referring to al-silm (peace), because it is feminine. If you wish you make it refer to the deed (al-faʿla), as He said ﴿إنّ رَبّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, where only a verb was mentioned before it, so the hāʾ refers to the deed.

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: between the hearts of the Anṣār, of al-Aws and al-Khazraj. There had been war between them, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Medina, Allah set right relations between them through him and through Islam.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «أصح», evidently for «أصلح» ("set right").]

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ﴾: the exegesis came as: Allah suffices you and suffices those who follow you. So the position of the kāf in (حسبك) is genitive (khafḍ), and (مَنْ) is in the position of the accusative according to the exegesis, as the poet said:
إذا كانت الهيجاء وانشقّتِ العصا * فحسبُك والضَّحاكَ سيفٌ مُهَنّد
(When war breaks out and the staff [of unity] is split, an Indian sword suffices you and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.)
It is not frequent in their speech to say حسبك وأخاك until they say حسبك وحسب أخيك; but we allowed it because in (حسبك) there is the sense of a verb acting [on an object], so we referred it back to the meaning of the kāf, not to its form, as in His saying ﴿إنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ﴾, where He referred الأهل back to the meaning of the kāf.
If you wish, you make (مَنْ) in the position of the nominative, and that is the dearer of the two options to me, because the recitation points to the nominative sense; do you not see that He said: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾: the Prophet ﷺ used to send his Companions on campaigns on the basis that ten were for a hundred and one for ten, and so they were. Then it became hard for them that one should be matched against ten, so there was revealed: ﴿ٱلآنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوۤاْ أَلْفَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلآنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوۤاْ أَلْفَيْنِ﴾: so Allah made clear their strength first and last. Al-Kisāʾī held this view and put (من) in the nominative.
[Translator's note: the last sentence appears to belong to the discussion of ﴿وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ﴾ in verse 64; it is translated where the source places it.]

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَىٰ﴾: its meaning is: it was not proper for him on the day of Badr to accept ransom for the captives ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُثْخِنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: until he prevails over many of those on the earth. Then there was revealed His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾: concerning the ransom of the captives and the spoils. It has also been read (أَُسارى), and each is correct. And His saying (أَن يَّكُونَ) [is read] with the masculine and the feminine [يكون / تكون], like His saying (يَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتهُم) and (تَشْهَدُ).

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, then He said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ﴾: in inheritance. They used to inherit from one another to the exclusion of their relatives who had not emigrated.
That is His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُواْ مَا لَكُمْ مِّن وَلاَيَتِهِم﴾, meaning: of their inheritances.
Putting a kasra on the wāw in al-wilāya is more pleasing to me than a fatḥa, because it is mostly given a fatḥa when it has the meaning of support (nuṣra). Al-Kisāʾī used to read it with a fatḥa, taking it to mean support, and I do not think he knew the exegesis. For walītuhu wilāyatan (I took charge of it) they choose the kasra; but we have heard both, with fatḥa and kasra, in both their meanings. The poet said:
دعِيهمْ فَهُمْ أَلْبٌ عَلَىَّ وِلايةٌ * وحَفْرُهُمُ أَنْ يَعْلَموا ذاكَ دائب
(Leave them, for they are banded together against me in alliance, and their digging to find that out is unceasing.)
Then there was revealed afterwards: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ مَعَكُمْ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مِنكُمْ وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾: if you do not inherit from one another on the basis of kinship, there will be discord. It is also mentioned that it concerns support: if you do not support one another, there will be discord.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ مَعَكُمْ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مِنكُمْ وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾: so they inherited from one another, and this latter verse abrogated the verse before it. That is that His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾.
[Translator's note: the last sentence breaks off in the source; translated as it stands.]

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَنْفَالِ﴾: it was revealed concerning the spoils (anfāl) of the people of Badr. That is because when the Prophet ﷺ saw how few the people were and their dislike of fighting, he said: "Whoever kills a man shall have such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive shall have such-and-such."
When he had finished with the people of Badr, Saʿd ibn Muʿādh stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you give these what you named for them, many of the Muslims will remain with nothing." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿قُلِ ٱلأَنفَالُ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾: he does with them what he wills. So they fell silent, with some dislike of that in their hearts.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾: this hāʾ is for the reinforcing (al-irdāf): Allah did not make the reinforcing ﴿إِلاَّ بُشْرَىٰ﴾.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِّنْهُ﴾: the Muslims spent the night of Badr without water, and they awoke in a state of major ritual impurity (janāba). Satan whispered to them, saying: "You claim that you are on the religion of Allah, yet you are without water while your enemy is at the water, and you pray in a state of janāba!" So Allah sent the sky upon them, and they drank and washed; and Allah removed from them the defilement (rijz) of Satan, meaning his whispering. They were in sand in which the feet sank, and the rain made it firm until men could tread firmly on it. That is His saying: ﴿وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلأَقْدَامَ﴾.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾: an angel would come to a man among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ and say: "I heard these people — meaning Abū Sufyān and his companions — saying: By Allah, if they charge at us, we shall be routed." Then the Muslims would tell one another of that, and their spirits would be strengthened. That is His inspiring the angels.
His saying: ﴿فَٱضْرِبُواْ فَوْقَ ٱلأَعْنَاقِ﴾: He taught them the places to strike, and said: strike the heads, the hands and the feet.
That is His saying: ﴿وَٱضْرِبُواْ مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ﴾.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾: He addressed the polytheists.
Then He said: ﴿وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾: (أَنّ) is accusative from two directions.
As for one of them: that is "because (بأن) the disbelievers have the punishment of the Fire"; the bāʾ was dropped and so it became accusative. The other accusative is that you imply a verb, as in the saying of the poet:
تسمع للأحشاء منه لغطا * ولليدين جُسْأَةً وبَدَدَا
(You hear a clamour from his insides, and [see] in his two forelegs stiffness and a wide stance.)
He implied (and you see in the two forelegs). Likewise He said ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾, and know ﴿َأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾. And if you wish you may make (أن) in the position of the nominative, meaning: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾, and that is ﴿أَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾. Similar to it in the Book of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿خَتَمَ اللّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةً﴾: ʿĀṣim read it so, according to what al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to me; and he claimed that ʿĀṣim took it from him twice with the accusative [Translator's note: the source has "بانصب", a misprint for بالنصب]. And likewise His saying: ﴿وحُورٌ عِينٌ﴾.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مُتَحَرِّفاً لِّقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ﴾: it is an exception, and the one withdrawing (al-mutaḥayyiz) is other than مَن. And if you wish you may make it part of the description of مَن, and it is on the pattern of your saying: "except that he turns his back on them", meaning to return to the attack; as you say in speech: "عبدالله يأتيك إلاّ ماشيا" ("ʿAbdallāh will come to you, unless on foot") and "يأتيك إلا أن تمنعه الرحلة" ("he will come to you unless the journey prevents him"). And (إلا) here does not have the sense of His saying ﴿إلى طعام غيرَ ناظرين إنَاهُ﴾, because (غير) [there] follows the pattern of (لا), not the pattern of (إلا).

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمَآ أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ despite their reluctance: so proceed with Allah's command concerning the spoils as you proceeded with your setting out while they were reluctant.
And it is said about it: they ask you about the spoils just as they disputed with you on the day of Badr and said: "You brought us out for booty and did not tell us of fighting so that we might prepare for it." That is His saying: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾

farraa:6-7.t:
His saying: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾; and His saying: ﴿فاتَّقُوا الله وَأَصْلِحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾: He commanded the Muslims to share with one another in the spoils after they had been granted to them, as a command that is not obligatory.
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحْدَى ٱلطَّائِفَتِيْنِ﴾, then He said ﴿أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ﴾: He put (إحدى الطائفتين) in the accusative by "يعد", then repeated it, on the sense of: He promises you that one of the two parties is yours; as He said: ﴿فهل ينظرون إِلا الساعة﴾, then said: ﴿أَن تَأْتِيهم بغتة﴾: أن is in the position of the accusative just as الساعة was put in the accusative. And His saying: ﴿ولولا رِجال مؤمِنون ونِساء مؤمِنات﴾: He put them in the nominative by "لولا", then said: ﴿أَن تطئوهم﴾, so أن is in the position of the nominative by "لولا".

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿ بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾, and it is read (مُرْدَفين). As for (مردِفين), it means following one another; and (مردَفين): it was done to them [i.e. they were made to follow].

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The clause «فاتقوا الله» is resumptive. «بينكم»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with kasra. The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if you are believers, then fear Allah".

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The conditional clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the noun relative, with no grammatical position. «زادتهم إيمانا»: a past verb, and its two objects are the hāʾ and «إيمانا». The clause «يتوكلون» is conjoined to the conditional clause «وإذا تليت عليهم ...», with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «الذين يقيمون»: the relative noun is a badal (substitute) from the preceding relative noun, in the position of the nominative. The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينفقون».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «هم»: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. «حقا»: stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "a true belief". «عند ربهم»: the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «درجات». The clause «لهم درجات» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «المؤمنون», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «كما»: the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "the spoils are established for Allah with an establishment like the establishment of your being brought out", and «ما» is maṣdariyya. «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «أخرجك». The clause «وإن فريقًا من المؤمنين لكارهون» is a ḥāl from the kāf in «أخرجك», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: His words «بعدما تبيَّن»: «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «يجادلونك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «كارهون», and the clause «كأنما يساقون» is a second ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «كارهون»; «كأنما» is a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa), with no governing effect. The clause «وهم ينظرون» is a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), from the wāw in «يُساقون».

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «وإذ يعدكم» is resumptive, and the clause «يعدكم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «إذ» is an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) اذكر. The interpreted maṣdar «أنها لكم» is a badal (substitute) from «إحدى», i.e. "its being yours". The interpreted maṣdar «أن غير ذات» is the object of «ودَّ». The interpreted maṣdar «أن يحق» is the object of «يريد».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: His words «ليحق»: the lām is causal, and the verb is accusative by أن optionally concealed after the lām; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقطع», and «الحق» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). His words «ولو كره»: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); this ḥāl (circumstantial) is conjoined to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl, the implied form being: "in every state, even in this state"; this is for exhausting all the states. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the clause is a ḥāl from the establishing understood from his words «ليحق».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) اذكر, and the clause «تستغيثون» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The preposition «من الملائكة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of ألف, and «مردفين» is a second naʿt of ألف. The interpreted maṣdar «أني ممدكم» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «إلا» is for restriction, and «بشرى» is the second object of «جعله». His words «ولتطمئن»: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is causal, and the verb is accusative by أن optionally concealed; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām, conjoined to «بشرى». It was made genitive because the condition of the agent being the same is not met: the agent of the making is Allah, while the agent of the reassurance is the hearts. The preposition «من عند الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), «إلا» is for restriction, and the clause «وما النصر إلا من عند الله» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «إذ يغشيكم»: a badal (substitute) from «إذ» in verse 9, and «أمنة» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The preposition «من السماء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ماء». The interpreted maṣdar «ليطهركم» is genitive by the lām, attached to «يُنزل», and the interpreted maṣdar «وليربط» is conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar, i.e. "for purifying and for strengthening".

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «إذ يوحي»: an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) from {إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ}, and the interpreted maṣdar «أني معكم» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ. The clause «فثبِّتوا» is conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar «أني معكم». The clause «سألقي» is parenthetical between the two conjoined verbs, and the clause «فاضربوا» is conjoined to «فثبتوا», in the position of the jussive [Translator's note: so in the source]. The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كل», and «كل» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The interpreted maṣdar «بأنهم شاقوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «ذلك». «من» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ, and the clause «ومن يشاقق» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (ذلكم فذوقوه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] A demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "the punishment"; the lām is for distance, and «كم» is for address. His words «فذوقوه»: the fāʾ is for conjunction, and an imperative verb; the clause «فذوقوه» is conjoined to the clause «ذلكم العقاب». The wāw in «وأن للكافرين» is a conjunction; the interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "decreed", i.e. "the punishment's being for the disbelievers is decreed". The clause of the interpreted maṣdar and its khabar is conjoined to the resumptive clause «ذلكم العقاب».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The conditional clause is the answer to the vocative, resumptive. «زحفا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «الأدبار» is a second object. The clause «لقيتم» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «من»: a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). «يومئذ»: «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يولِّهم»; «إذٍ» is an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the tanwīn compensates for a clause. «دبره» is a second object. «إلا» is for restriction. «متحرفا»: excepted from the generality of states; it is originally an exception from an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "whoever turns them his back in any state at all except such-and-such a state". The preposition «لقتال» is attached to «متحرفا», and the preposition «من الله» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «غضب». The clause «مأواه جهنم» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). His words «وبئس المصير»: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "Hell", and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The fāʾ in «فلم» is resumptive. «إذ رميت» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رميت». The clause «ولكن الله قتلهم» is conjoined to the clause «لم تقتلوهم», the clause «وما رميت» is conjoined to the clause «لم تقتلوهم», and the clause «ولكن الله رمى» is conjoined to the clause «وما رميت». His words «وليبلي»: an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām, attached to an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. "and He did that in order to test". The clause «وفعل ذلك» is conjoined to the clause «ولكن الله رمى». His words «بلاء»: stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «ذلكم»: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "the matter"; the clause «ذلكم الأمر» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. «وأن الله»: the wāw is a conjunction, then an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) and its noun; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to the nominal clause, i.e. «ذلكم الأمر وأن الله موهن».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: His words «شيئا»: stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "an availing, little or much". His words «ولو كثرت»: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), conjoining to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the implied form is: "in every state, even in this state"; this is for exhausting all the states. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "even if it were many, it would not avail you". The clause «ولو كثرت» is a ḥāl from «فئتكم». The interpreted maṣdar «وأن الله ...» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām, i.e. "He did such-and-such because Allah..."; the implied clause «فعل» is conjoined to the clause «لن تغني».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «يا أيها الذين»: the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma; «ها» is for drawing attention, and the relative noun is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The clause «وأنتم تسمعون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تَوَلَّوا».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The clause «وهم لا يسمعون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun «نا» in «سمعنا».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «عند الله»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شر». «الصم البكم» are two khabars (predicates) of «إن», and the relative noun is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition «فيهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «خيرًا». The clause «ولو علم الله» is conjoined to the clause {إِنَّ شَرَّ}, and the clause «ولو أسمعهم» is conjoined to the clause «لو علم الله». The clause «وهم معرضون» is a ḥāl from the wāw in «تولَّوا», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: «إذا»: purely adverbial, attached to (mutaʿalliq) استجيبوا, and the clause «دعاكم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The interpreted maṣdar «أن الله يحول» takes the place of the two objects of علم, and the second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to the first, in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: His words «لا تصيبن»: «لا» is prohibitive, and the verb is an imperfect, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive; the nūn has no grammatical position, and the fāʿil (agent) is the pronoun "it". The relative noun is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The prohibition is in form addressed to the calamity and in meaning to those addressed. The clause is governed by an omitted saying, and that saying is the adjective, i.e. "a trial about which it is said: «لا تصيبن»", meaning: "do not engage in causes through which a calamity will strike you that does not single out the wrongdoers among you". The clause «لا تصيبن» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative; the implied form is: "a trial about which such-and-such is said". The preposition «منكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw, i.e. "they did wrong, being from among you". «خاصة» is a ḥāl from the object, which is the relative noun, i.e. "it will not strike the wrongdoers exclusively; rather it will include them and include others".

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «أنتم قليل» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «مستضعفون» is a second khabar (predicate), and the preposition after it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. The clause «تخافون» is a third khabar. The clause «لعلكم تشكرون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The interpreted maṣdar «أن يتخطفكم» is a mafʿūl bihi.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The clause «وأنتم تعلمون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «تخونوا».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أنما أموالكم» takes the place of the two objects of علم, and the second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to the first. The clause «عنده أجر» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن».

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: The conditional clause is the answer to the vocative, resumptive, and the clause «والله ذو الفضل» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: The clause «وإذ يمكر» is resumptive; «إذ» is the object of an implied (muqaddar) اذكر. The clause «يمكرون» is resumptive, and the clause «والله خير الماكرين» is conjoined to the clause «يمكر الله».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «لو نشاء لقلنا» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and likewise the clause «إن هذا إلا أساطير»; «إن» is negating, «إلا» is for restriction, and «أساطير» is the khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: His words «وإذ قالوا»: conjoined to «إذ» in verse 30. «اللهم»: the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the accusative; the mīm compensates for (يا). «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, «الحق» is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, and the preposition «من عندك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحق».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The lām in «ليعذبهم» is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and the verb is accusative by a concealed أن; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of kāna, the implied form being: "intending punishment". The clause «وأنت فيهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «يعذبهم», and the clause «وهم يستغفرون» is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «معذبهم», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: (وما لهم ألا يعذبهم الله) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition phrase is the khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition (في). The clause «وهم يصدون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «يعذبهم», and the clause «وما كانوا أولياءه» is conjoined to the clause «وهم يصدون». The clause «إن أولياؤه إلا المتقون» is resumptive; «إن» is negating and «إلا» is for restriction. The clause «ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون» is conjoined to the resumptive clause, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «عند البيت»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «صلاتهم». The clause «فذوقوا» is resumptive, and «ما» in his words «بما كنتم» is maṣdariyya; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to «فذوقوا».

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The interpreted maṣdar «ليصدوا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينفقون», and the preposition phrase is attached to the verb. The clause «فسينفقونها» is resumptive. The preposition «عليهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «حسرة». The preposition «إلى جهنم» is attached to the verb «يحشرون», and the clause of the relative noun is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The interpreted maṣdar «ليميز» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) {يُحْشَرُونَ}. «بعضه» is a badal (substitute) from «الخبيث». The preposition «على بعض» is attached to the second object of «يجعل». «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الخبيث», and the preposition «في جهنم» is attached to the second object of يجعل.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The clause «إن ينتهوا» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative, and «ما» is a relative noun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: «تكون»: a complete (tāmm) past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; «تكون» is an imperfect verb], and «فتنة» is its fāʿil (agent). «انتهوا» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on a ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the wāw is the fāʿil. The preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) «بصير».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن الله مولاكم» takes the place of the two objects of علم. The clause «نعم المولى» is resumptive, and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. "Allah".

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: «ما»: a relative noun, the noun of «أن»; the preposition «من شيء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». His words «فأن لله»: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), by likening the relative noun to the condition; the interpreted maṣdar is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "obligatory". The clause «إن كنتم» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. His words «يوم التقى»: a badal (substitute) from the first «يوم».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, the object of an implied (muqaddar) اذكروا, and the clause «أنتم بالعدوة» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of the genitive. His words «والركب أسفل منكم»: the wāw is a conjunction, «الركب» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «أسفل» is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the preposition «منكم» is attached to «أسفل». His words «ليقضي»: an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed أن [Translator's note: the source reads «مضمرة بالفعل», "concealed with the verb"; presumably "after the lām"], and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām, attached to the verb «تلاقيتم», implied. The clause «ولكن تلاقيتم» is conjoined to the conditional clause. The preposition «ليهلك» is a badal (substitute) from «ليقضي», and the relative noun «مَنْ» is the fāʿil (agent). The preposition «عن بينة» is attached to «يحيا».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «إذ»: an adverbial noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied (muqaddar) اذكر. «يريكهم» is an imperfect verb taking two objects, the kāf and the hāʾ; the preposition «في منامك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and «قليلا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ. The conditional clause is conjoined to the clause «يريكهم», in the position of the genitive. The lām in «لتنازعتم» is for added linking, and the preposition «في الأمر» is attached to «تنازعتم». The clause «ولكن الله سلَّم» is conjoined to the clause «ولو أراكهم», in the position of the genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The wāw is a conjunction; «إذ» is an adverbial noun conjoined to {إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ}. The wāw in «يريكموهم» is for lengthening (ishbāʿ), with no grammatical position. «إذ التقيتم»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. The interpreted maṣdar «ليقضي» is genitive, attached to «يقلِّلكم», and the clause «كان» is a naʿt (adjective) of «أمرا», in the position of the accusative. The clause «ترجع» is resumptive, and the preposition «إلى الله» is attached to «ترجع».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The conditional clause is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; the clause «لقيتم» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «كثيرا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The clause «لعلكم تفلحون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: His words «فتفشلوا»: the fāʾ is causal, and the verb is an imperfect, accusative by أن necessarily concealed after the fāʾ of causation; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "let there be no disputing among you, and so failure". The clause «تفشلوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: «بطرًا»: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). «ما» in his words «بما يعملون» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «والله بما يعملون محيط» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «إذ»: the object of an implied (muqaddar) اذكر, and the clause is resumptive. The preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and «اليوم» likewise; the preposition «من الناس» is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لكم». The clause «وإني جار لكم» is conjoined to the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl). The clause «فلما تراءت الفئتان» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «إذ زين», and the clause «إني أرى» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: «إذ يقول»: a badal (substitute) from «إذ» in the previous verse. «هؤلاء» is a demonstrative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «دينهم» is a fāʿil (agent) placed later. «مَن» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «يتوكل» is its khabar (predicate); the conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: «إذ»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ترى». «الذين» is a relative noun, an object placed first, and «الملائكة» is a fāʿil (agent) placed later. The clause «يضربون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الملائكة». The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "you would have seen a tremendous matter". «ذوقوا» is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted saying, in the position of the accusative, and the implied clause of saying «يقولون» is conjoined to the clause «يضربون», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The interpreted maṣdar «وأن الله» is conjoined to «ما», the genitive relative noun. «ظلام» is an intensive form, and the bāʾ in the khabar of laysa is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The preposition «كدأب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the implied form is: "the habit of these is like the habit". The clause «دأبهم كدأب» is resumptive, and the clause «كفروا» explains the habit.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: The interpreted maṣdar «بأن الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). «يك» is an imperfect abrogating verb (nāsikh), jussive (majzūm) with a sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn dropped for lightness; «مغيرًا» is the khabar of kāna, and «نعمة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «مُغَيِّرًا». The interpreted maṣdar «أن يغيِّروا» is genitive by «حتى», attached to «مغيرًا», and the preposition «بأنفسهم» is attached to the implied ṣila (relative clause). The interpreted maṣdar «وأن الله سميع» is conjoined to the preceding interpreted maṣdar «أن الله لم يكُ مُغيرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The preposition «كدأب»: the preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); the implied form is «دأبهم كدأب». The clause «كذَّبوا» explains the habit, with no grammatical position. The clause «وكل كانوا» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «دأبهم كدأب».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The adverb «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شَرّ», and «الذين» is the khabar (predicate) of inna. The clause «فهم لا يؤمنون» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) «كفروا», with no grammatical position, and the clause «لا يؤمنون» is the khabar of «هم».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: «الذين عاهدت»: a badal (substitute) from the preceding relative noun. The preposition «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun. The clause «وهم لا يتقون» is conjoined to the clause «ينقضون».

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: «فإمَّا تثقفنهم»: the fāʾ is a conjunction; «إما» is composed of the conditional «إنْ» and the redundant «ما»; the verb is an imperfect, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, in the position of the jussive; the clause is conjoined to {إِنَّ شَرَّ} .... The preposition «في الحرب» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تثقفنهم», and «خلفهم» is an adverb attached to the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause). The clause «لعلهم يذَّكَّرون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The preposition «من قوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «خيانة», and the preposition «على سواء» is attached to a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) and the object together. The clause «إن الله لا يحب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: His words «ولا يحسبن»: the wāw is resumptive, «لا» is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn, in the position of the jussive; its first object is omitted, its implied form being: "themselves", and the clause «سبقوا» is a second object. The clause «إنهم لا يعجزون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the preposition «من قوة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun. The clause «ترهبون» is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of «أعدوا». His words «وآخرين»: a noun conjoined to «عدوكم», and the preposition «من دونهم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of آخرين. The clause «لا تعلمونهم» is a second naʿt of آخرين, and the clause «الله يعلمهم» is a third naʿt. His words «وما تنفقوا من شيء»: the wāw is resumptive, «ما» is conditional, mafʿūl bihi, and the verb is jussive (majzūm); the preposition «من شيء» is attached to a naʿt of «ما», and the preposition «في سبيل» is attached to a naʿt of «شيء». The clause «وأنتم لا تظلمون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «إليكم», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The clause «إنه هو السميع» is resumptive; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه», and «السميع العليم» are two khabars (predicates) of «إن».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن يخدعوك» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «هو الذي» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The preposition «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause), and «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرض». The clause «ولكنَّ الله ألف» is conjoined to the clause «ما ألَّفْت», and the clause «إنه عزيز» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: «ومن اتبعك»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is an implied (muqaddar) (كذلك), and the preposition «من المؤمنين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in «اتبعك».

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The conditional clause is resumptive within the scope of the answer to the vocative. «عشرون» is the noun of يكن, and the tamyīz (specification) of the number has been omitted. «مائتين» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. The preposition «من الذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ألفًا», and the clause «لا يفقهون» is a naʿt of «قوم».

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «الآن»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خفف», indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. The interpreted maṣdar takes the place of the two objects of علم. The clause «فإن يكن» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. The preposition «بإذن الله» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in «يغلبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن يكون» is the noun of kāna, and the preposition «لنبي» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «تريدون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: «لولا»: a particle of non-occurrence because of occurrence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd), and «كتاب» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: "existing". The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», and the clause «سبق» is a second naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The fāʾ in «فكلوا» conjoins to something implied (muqaddar), i.e. "I have made the spoils lawful for you, so eat". The implied clause «أبحت» is resumptive. The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «كلوا». «حلالا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); it is originally an adjective of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "eat lawful food".

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «النبي»: ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The preposition «في أيديكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause), and the preposition «من الأسرى» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun. The conditional clause is the content of the speech (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative. The second «خيرًا» is a second object. The preposition «ممَّا» is attached to «خيرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «وإن يريدوا» is conjoined to the preceding answer to the vocative.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The clause «أولئك بعضهم أولياء بعض» is the khabar (predicate) of «إن». His words «ما لكم من ولايتهم من شيء»: «ما» is negating and inoperative; the preposition «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar, and the preposition «من ولايتهم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شيء»; «شيء» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «ما لكم شيء» is the khabar of «الذين». The interpreted maṣdar «حتى يهاجروا» is attached to an omitted khabar of «شيء». The clause «فعليكم النصر» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The preposition «إلا على قوم» is attached to a ḥāl from the omitted excepted, i.e. "except help being against a people". The clause «بينكم وبينهم ميثاق» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوم», in the position of the genitive.

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: «بعضهم»: a second mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «أولياء», and the clause «بعضهم أولياء بعض» is the khabar of «الذين». The clause «إن لا تفعلوه تكن» is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «تكن» is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb.

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The clause «أولئك هم المؤمنون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين»; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). «حقًا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "believers with a true belief". The clause «لهم مغفرة» is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذين».

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: «بعدُ» is indeclinable (mabnī) because it is cut off from annexation. His words «فأولئك»: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and it was attached to the clause of the khabar (predicate) by likening the relative noun to the condition; the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «بعضهم أولى ببعض» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «أولو». The preposition «ببعض» is attached to «أولى».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: The saying of the Exalted {ذَات بَيْنكُم}: the original form of ذات according to the Basrans is ذوات; the wāw was changed into an alif and then dropped because it was quiescent and the alif after it was quiescent, so ذات remained. This is shown by the saying of the Exalted in the dual: ذواتا أفنان, where the wāw returned to its original form. All the scholars and the Qurʾān readers pause on ذات with tāʾ, except Abū Ḥātim, who allowed pausing on it with hāʾ. Quṭrub said: the pause on ذات is with hāʾ wherever it occurs, because it is the hāʾ of the feminine of ذي مال ("possessor of wealth").

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying {وجلت قُلُوبهم}: the imperfect of وجل is يوجل. Among the Arabs there are those who say ييجل, replacing the wāw with yāʾ; among them are those who put kasra on the first yāʾ; and among them are those who put fatḥa on the first yāʾ and replace the second with an alif — just as they said رأيت الزيدان, replacing the yāʾ with an alif — so they say ياجل.
«[Translator's note: the printed text reads «يَا جلّ»; the intended form is evidently ياجل.]»

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying {كَمَا أخرجك رَبك من بَيْتك}: the kāf in كما is in the position of the accusative (naṣb), a naʿt (adjective) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of يجادلونك, i.e. "a disputing like…". It has been said that it is a naʿt of a maṣdar indicated by the meaning of the speech, its implied form being: "Say: the spoils are established for Allah and the Messenger, an establishing like [the way] your Lord brought you out". It has been said that it is a naʿt of حقا, i.e. "they are the believers truly, like…". It has been said that the kāf is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), the implied form being: "As your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth, so fear Allah", so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And it has been said that the kāf has the meaning of the wāw of oath, i.e. "the spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger — by Him who brought you out".
«[Translator's note: the text has «نعت لحق»; the reference is to the word حَقًّا in verse 4.]»

mekki-muskil:7-7.t:
His saying {إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لكم}: أنّ is a badal (substitute) of إحدى, and it is badal al-ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion). إحدى is the second object of يعد, its implied form being: "And when Allah promised you possession of one of the two parties". An omitted muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) was assumed only because a promise does not fall upon concrete entities; it falls only upon events.
His saying {وَإِذ يَعدكُم}: إذ is in the position of the accusative by an implied (muḍmar) verb, its implied form being: "And remember, O Muhammad, when He promised you".
It is related from ʿĀṣim that he read {بِأَلف من الْمَلَائِكَة} [as بآلُفٍ], making it the plural of ألف — a فَعْل on the pattern أفعُل, like فلس and أفلس. The confirmation of this reading is the saying of the Exalted بخمسة آلاف: آلُف is the plural of ألف for fewer than ten, and it refers to the five thousand mentioned in Āl ʿImrān.
«[Translator's note: the bracketed form بآلُفٍ is added for clarity from the explanation that follows; the text quotes the verse in its usual form.]»

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying {مُردفِينَ}: whoever reads it with fatḥa on the dāl makes it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in ممدكم, or a naʿt (adjective) of ألف, its implied form being: "He reinforces you, followed up, with a thousand". The hāʾ in جعله refers back to the thousand (الألف), because it is masculine. It has been said that it refers to the following-up (الإرداف), indicated by His saying مردفين; it has been said that it refers to the reinforcement (الإمداد), indicated by His saying ممدكم; and it has been said that it refers to the acceptance of the supplication, indicated by the saying of the Exalted فاستجاب لكم. Likewise the hāʾ in به admits all of these aspects, and it may also refer to the good tidings (البشرى), because it has the meaning of rejoicing at good news (الاستبشار).
Whoever reads مردفين with kasra on the dāl makes it a ṣifa (adjective) of ألف, its meaning being: they were followed up by another number behind them, and the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, namely "a number". It has also been said that the meaning of the adjective is that they came after despair, i.e. they followed them up after they had called for help. Abū ʿUbayda reported that ردفني and أردفني both mean "he followed me". Most of the grammarians hold that أردفه means "he carried him behind him" and ردفه means "he followed him"; al-Naḥḥās also reported this from Abū ʿUbayd. On this basis it is not good for it to be an adjective of the angels, since it is not known of their description that they carried anyone of the people behind them.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t: His saying {أَمَنَة}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying {فَوق الْأَعْنَاق}, i.e. the heads. فوق, according to al-Akhfash, is redundant (zāʾida), the meaning being "strike the necks". Al-Mubarrad said: فوق indicates the permissibility of striking their faces, because they are above the necks.
And His saying {كل بنان} means the fingers and other limbs.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying {ذَلِك بِأَنَّهُم}: ذلك is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "the matter is that" or "that is the matter".
His saying {وَمن يُشَاقق الله}: من is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is فإن الله شديد العقاب. The referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, its implied form being: "then Allah is severe in punishment towards him".

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying {وَأَن للْكَافِرِينَ}: أنّ is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذلكم, and ذلكم is in the position of the nominative like the ذلك before it. Al-Farrāʾ said: وأن للكافرين is in the position of the accusative on the assumption of the omission of the preposition, i.e. "and because the disbelievers have…". It is also permissible to imply "and know that…". The hāʾ in فذوقوه refers back to ذلكم, and that is an allusion to the killing on the day of Badr.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying {زحفا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying {متحرفا} and {متحيزا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied nominative pronoun in يولهم.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {مِنْهُ بلَاء}: the hāʾ in منه refers back to the victory over the polytheists; it has also been said: to the throwing.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His saying {وَأَن الله}: أنّ is in the position of the accusative on the assumption "and because Allah…"; reading it with kasra (إنّ) as a new beginning (istiʾnāf) is also permissible.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His saying {وتخونوا أماناتكم}: jussive (majzūm) by conjunction with لا تخونوا; or, if you wish, it is accusative (naṣb) as the answer to the prohibition with the wāw.
His saying {وَأَنْتُم تَسْمَعُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun in تولوا; and similar to it is وهم معرضون.
«[Translator's note: the verse وأنتم تسمعون with تولوا is 8:20, not 8:27; the text is translated as it stands.]»

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His saying {هُوَ الْحق}: هو is a separating pronoun (fāṣila) announcing that the khabar (predicate) is definite or close to definite. It has been said that it was introduced to announce that كان is not in the sense of "occurred" and "happened", and that the khabar is still awaited. It has been said that it was introduced to announce that what follows it is a khabar, not a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it. Al-Akhfash said: هو is redundant (zāʾida), just as ما was made redundant in فبما رحمة. The Kufans said: هو is an ʿimād (support pronoun).
«[Translator's note: the text reads «خبر بنعت», evidently for «خبر لا نعت» ("a predicate, not an adjective"), and is translated accordingly.]»

mekki-muskil:34-34.t:
His saying {أَلا يعذبهم الله}: أن is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "from not punishing them" (من أن لا يعذبهم). Al-Akhfash mentioned that أن is redundant (zāʾida), yet he has made the verb accusative by it, and that is not the rule for a redundant particle.
And His saying {وهم يصدون}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied accusative pronoun in يعذبهم.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t:
His saying {وتصدية}: it is from صدّ يصِدّ when one clamours, and its origin is تصددة; one of the two dāls was replaced by a yāʾ. The meaning of تصدية is clamouring with clapping. It has been said that it is from صدّ يصُدّ when one prevents. And it has been said that it is from الصدى, the echo that answers your voice from a mountain or the air: as though the one who claps answers with his clapping someone who intends [to pray] in his prayer; on this view the yāʾ is radical.
المكاء is whistling; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الدعاء, and the hamza is a substitute for a wāw, because they say مكا يمكو when one blows.
Al-Aʿmash read وما كان صلاتهم with the accusative, and إلا مكاء وتصدية with the nominative. This is not permissible except in poetry out of necessity, because the noun of كان is the definite one and its khabar (predicate) is the indefinite one, according to the principles of speech, reasoning and meaning.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {أَنما غَنِمْتُم}: ما has the sense of الذي (relative noun), and the hāʾ is omitted from the ṣila (relative clause), its implied form being غنمتموه. The khabar (predicate) is فأن لله خمسه. The reason أن has fatḥa here is that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "then its ruling is that to Allah belongs its fifth". It has been said that [the second] أن emphasises the first, but this is not permissible, because the first would then remain without a khabar, and because the fāʾ would intervene between the emphasised word and its tawkīd (emphasis), and its being redundant is not good in a place such as this.

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His saying {والركب أَسْفَل مِنْكُم}: أسفل is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted adverb of place (ẓarf), its implied form being "and the caravan in a place lower than you". Al-Akhfash, al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī allowed أسفلُ in the nominative, on the assumption of something omitted at the start of the phrase, its implied form being "and the place of the caravan is lower than you".
His saying {من حييّ}: whoever pronounces the two yāʾs separately [حَيِيَ] makes the past follow the imperfect. Since assimilation (idghām) is not permitted in the imperfect — because its vowel is not fixed, shifting from nominative to accusative or to elision in the jussive — he treated the past like it, even though the vowel of its final radical is fixed; moreover the final radical of the past is also made quiescent when it is joined to a nominative pronoun, so in its changeability it has become like the final radical of the imperfect, and it was treated like it in being pronounced separately. As for whoever assimilates [حَيَّ], it is to distinguish between that whose final radical has a fixed vowel, such as the past, and that whose final radical has a shifting vowel, such as the imperfect in His saying أن يحيي الموتى — this may not be assimilated. So he assimilated the past because of the meeting of two identical letters, and assimilation is good because of the fixedness of the vowel on its final radical. Al-Farrāʾ alone allowed assimilation in the imperfect; no one else allowed it.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t:
His saying {إِذْ يريكهم}: the governing word of إذ is an implied verb, its implied form being: "And remember, O Muhammad, when He showed them to you".
«[Translator's note: the text reads «ذَا يريكهم», evidently for «إذ يريكهم».]»

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: And His saying {وَإِذ يريكموهم}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first إذ. The wāw returned with the plural mīm when a pronoun is attached, because a pronoun restores elided letters to their original forms. Yūnus allowed dropping the wāw with the pronoun: he allowed يريكمهم with the mīm quiescent, and with it voweled with ḍamma without a wāw. Keeping it is better and more eloquent, and the Qurʾān came with it.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {بطرا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). البطر is to use the blessings of Allah as strength for acts of disobedience.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His saying {جَار}: جار is pluralised as أجوار for a small number, جيران for a large number, and also جيرة.

mekki-muskil:50-50.t: His saying {يضْربُونَ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the angels; and if you made it a ḥāl from الذين كفروا, that would be permissible. But if in the place of يضربون there were ضاربين, it would not be permissible until the pronoun were made overt, because when an active participle (ism fāʿil) runs as an adjective, a ḥāl, a khabar (predicate) or a conjunct of someone other than the one to whom it belongs, its agent pronoun may not be latent in it; it must be made overt. If you said رأيت رجلا معه امرأة ضاربها غدا أو الساعة ("I saw a man with a woman, beating her tomorrow or now"), and you put ضاربها in the nominative as an adjective of the woman, it would not be permissible until you said ضاربها هو, because the action is not hers. If you put it in the accusative as an adjective of the man, it is permissible and you would not need to make the pronoun overt, because the action is his. And if in the place of ضاربها there were يضربها, it would be permissible in both ways and there would be no need to make any pronoun overt.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t:
His saying {وَأَن الله لَيْسَ بظلام للعبيد}: أنّ is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to ما in His saying بما قدمت; or, if you wish, in the position of the nominative on إلى ذلك, or by implying وذلك.
«[Translator's note: «على إلى ذلك» is as printed and appears corrupt; perhaps «عطفًا على ذلك» ("conjoined to ذلك") is intended.]»

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His saying {كدأب آل فِرْعَوْن}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: "We did that to them, a doing like Our custom with the people of Pharaoh when they disbelieved". الدأب is custom. The second [occurrence] is like it, except that the first concerns the custom in punishing and the second the custom in changing; the implied form of the second is: "We changed [things] for them when they changed, a changing like Our custom with the people of Pharaoh when they denied".

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {فانبذ إِلَيْهِم على سَوَاء}: the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, its implied form being: "then throw back to them the covenant and fight them upon a notification from you to them". In the beginning of the verse there is another omission, its implied form being: "And if you fear treachery from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then throw back to them that covenant", i.e. return it to them if you fear their breaking the covenant, and fight them upon a notification from you to them. This is among the subtle inimitability of the Qurʾān and its concision, since it has gathered many meanings of commands and reports in a brief wording.

mekki-muskil:59-59.t:
His saying {وَلَا يَحسبن الَّذين كفرُوا سبقوا}: whoever reads it with tāʾ makes it an address to the Prophet ﷺ, because addressing him has preceded at the beginning of the passage; الذين is the first object and سبقوا is in the position of the second object. Whoever reads it with yāʾ makes it [the verb] of the disbelievers, so it contains their pronoun, because they were mentioned earlier in His saying الذين كفروا فهم لا يؤمنون, and in His saying ثم ينقضون, ولا يتقون, لعلهم يذكرون, and His saying إليهم; so the first object is implied and سبقوا is in the position of the second, its implied form being: "And let not those who disbelieve think themselves to have outstripped". It has been said that أن is implied with سبقوا, and it stands in place of the two objects, as it does in His saying أحسب الناس أن يتركوا; its implied form being "and let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped". Sībawayh said concerning the saying of the Exalted أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد that its implied form is أن أعبد; then أن was dropped and the verb became nominative. It has been said that the agent in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ is the Prophet, upon him be peace, so it is like the reading with tāʾ: الذين كفروا and سبقوا are the two objects of حسب. It has been said that the agent of حسب is implied in it, its implied form being "and let not those behind them think those who disbelieve to have outstripped", so الذين كفروا and سبقوا are the two objects of حسب.
Whoever reads أنهم لا يعجزون with fatḥa makes the speech connected to what precedes it, its implied form being "they have outstripped because they…", so أنّ is in the position of the accusative by the omission of the preposition; its meaning is: "And let not those who disbelieve think that they have escaped Allah, because they do not escape Allah". Whoever reads إنّ with kasra does so on the basis of a new beginning and a break [from what precedes].
«[Translator's note: the meaning-gloss «فاتوا من الله لأنهم لا يفوتون الله» is translated as printed.]»

mekki-muskil:60-60.t: His saying {وَآخَرين من دونهم}: accusative, conjoined to عدو الله.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t:
His saying {حَسبك الله وَمن اتبعك}: من is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the meaning of the kāf in حسبك الله, because in interpretation it is in the position of the accusative, since the meaning of حسبك الله is "Allah suffices you"; so من was conjoined according to the meaning. It has been said that من is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the name of Allah the Exalted; or as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) implied, i.e. "and those of the believers who follow you are likewise".
