(الفاء) conjunction [Note: Or it is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar, because the mubtadaʾ resembles the conditional.]; (إن) a conditional particle governing the jussive; (ما) a redundant particle; (تثقفنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) … and (النون) is for emphasis, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta"; (هم) mafʿūl bihi; (في الحرب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تثقفنّهم); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition; (شرّد) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (الباء) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (شرّ), the bāʾ being of causation [Translator's note: so in the source, evidently for «شرّد»]; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (خلف) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of «من», and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogating particle —, and (هم) a pronoun, the noun of laʿalla, in the position of the accusative; (يذّكّرون) like «يؤمنون».
The clause «تثقفنّهم …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «إنّ شرّ الدواب».
The clause «شرّد بهم» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition.
The clause «لعلّهم يذّكّرون» has no grammatical position, giving the reason — or an explanatory resumption —. The clause «يذّكّرون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of laʿalla.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(يسألون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn – and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the position of the accusative; (عن الأنفال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسألون), (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «you» (أنت); (الأنفال) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); (الواو) conjunctive; (الرسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr); (الفاء) to link the apodosis to an implied condition; (اتّقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunctive; (أصلحوا) like اتّقوا; (ذات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (بين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (أطيعوا) like اتقوا; (الله) the Name of Majesty, like the first; (الواو) conjunctive; (رسول) conjoined to the Name of Majesty, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) an incomplete past verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) a pronoun in the position of the nominative as ism of kāna; (مؤمنين) khabar of kāna, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «يسألونك..» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «الأنفال لله ...» is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of saying).
The clause «اتقوا الله ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. if you believe in this, then fear Allah.
The clause «أصلحوا ...» is conjoined to the clause اتّقوا الله.
The clause «أطيعوا ...» is conjoined to the clause اتّقوا الله.
The clause «كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied condition.. and the apodosis of the second condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: if you are believers, then fear Allah and set right.. and obey.

* Morphology:
(الأنفال): plural of نفل, a noun meaning spoils of war; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and the pattern of الأنفال is أفعال.

* Benefits:
1- The root (سأل): if the asking is about intellectual or abstract matters, the verb is made transitive with «عن», as in the verse «يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَنْفالِ», i.e. about their ruling; and if it is to request a material thing, it takes two objects, e.g.: سألت الكريم معونة للفقراء (I asked the generous man for help for the poor).
2- From the story of the spoils (al-anfāl): «setting right relations between you» (إصلاح ذات البين). ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said: The verse of al-Anfāl was revealed about us – the company of those who were present at Badr – when we had differed over the division of «the spoils» (النفل), which were our booty on the day of Badr, and our conduct had turned bad over it. So Allah took it out of our hands and gave it to the Messenger of Allah, who divided it justly among the Muslims; and in that was the fear of Allah, obedience to His Messenger, and the setting right of relations between them.

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) a restraining [mā] and the restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (المؤمنون) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis وجلت..; (ذكر) past verb, passive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (وجلت) past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine; (قلوب) fāʿil (agent), nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (إذا تليت.. آياته) like ذكر الله, and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تليت), (زادت) like وجلت, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «it» (هي), i.e. the verses, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إيمانا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الواو) conjunctive; (على ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتوكّلون), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يتوكّلون) like يسألون [Note: In verse (1) of this sūra.].
The clause «المؤمنون الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ذكر الله» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «وجلت قلوبهم» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تليت.. آياته» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «زادتهم ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause of the second condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the first condition.
The clause «يتوكّلون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the first condition, which is the ṣila clause [Note: It may be cut off as a resumption, and it may be in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of زادتهم.
(2, 3) In verse (1) of this sūra.].
(الذين) badal (substitute) of the first relative – or its naʿt (adjective) –; (يقيمون) like يسألون (2), (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (من) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينفقون), (رزقنا) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) a pronoun, fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (ينفقون) like يسألون (3).
The clause «يقيمون ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «رزقناهم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «ينفقون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يقيمون.
(أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) a particle of address; (هم) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar is المؤمنون, the nominal clause being the khabar of أولئك.] (المؤمنون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (حقّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) confirming the content of the preceding «volume» (المجلد) [Translator's note: so in the source; الجملة («clause») is evidently meant.] [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), being its adjective, i.e. the believers with a true faith.], (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; (درجات) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to درجات in the sense of rewards [Note: Or attached to an omitted naʿt of درجات.], (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (مغفرة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to درجات, nominative, and likewise (رزق); (كريم) naʿt of رزق, nominative.
The clause «أولئك.. المؤمنون» has no grammatical position: explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لهم درجات ...» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the pronoun latent in (المؤمنون).

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الكاف) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (أخرج) past verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من بيت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أخرجك), and (الكاف) like the last; (بالحقّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of أخرجك, i.e. clothed with the truth [Note: Or attached to the verb أخرجك, i.e. He brought you out because of the truth that would become manifest.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما أخرجك) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «the situation» or «your division of the spoils» [Note: The preposition phrase may be attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. the spoils were established with an establishing like your bringing out with the truth.. There are other views on the attachment of the preposition phrase; Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr made them fifteen views transmitted from the exegetes, among them: – attaching it to a mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by أصلحوا, i.e. set right relations between you with a setting right like your bringing out from your house, with a shift (iltifāt) in it from addressing the group to addressing the individual. b- or to a mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by أطيعوا, i.e. obey Allah and His Messenger like your bringing out from your house with the truth, i.e. a realised obedience. c- or to a mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by يتوكّلون, i.e. they rely with a reliance like your bringing out. d- or it is an adjective of (حقّا) from their saying هم المؤمنون حقا, i.e. truly, like the bringing out.. e- or to a mafʿūl muṭlaq governed by كارهون, i.e. they dislike with a dislike like your bringing out ...
Abū Ḥayyān rejected all of that, saying: «... Before writing down these views in al-Baḥr, when none of them had settled in my mind, I saw in a dream that I was walking with a man, discussing the verse with him, and I said to him: Nothing as problematic as this has come to me in the Qur'an; perhaps there is something omitted by which the meaning becomes sound, and I have not found anything substantial on it from any of the exegetes. Then I said to him: That omitted thing is «your victory» (نصرك). That man and I both found this derivation good; then I woke from sleep while remembering it ...» etc.].
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) –; (فريقا) ism of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (فريقا), (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (كارهون) khabar of inna, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «أخرجك ربّك ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī).
The clause «إنّ فريقا.. كارهون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the object pronoun in (أخرجك).
(يجادلون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (في الحقّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb يجادلون; (بعد) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يجادلون), (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (تبيّن) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «it» (هو), i.e. the truth, which is the fighting.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبيّن..) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(كأنّما) a restraining [mā] and the restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (يساقون) imperfect verb, passive, nominative..
and the wāw is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (إلى الموت) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يساقون), (الواو) circumstantial; (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ; (ينظرون) like يجادلون.
The clause «يجادلونك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: It may be a ḥāl of the pronoun in كارهون.].
The clause «يساقون ...» has no grammatical position: another resumption [Note: It may be a second ḥāl of the pronoun of كارهون.].
The clause «هم ينظرون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «ينظرون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.

* Rhetoric:
Representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in the noble verse, where his – upon him be peace – being singled out with the spoils, and the entrusting of their matter to his judgment as regards reward and recompense, is likened to his being brought out of his house obedient to Allah the Exalted, hearing His command, content with His judgment, despite the believers' dislike of that in obedience. So Allah the Exalted likened his reward with this distinction to his approved obedience: just as his obedience reached the utmost in the kind of acts of obedience, so too Allah's rewarding of him reached the utmost in the genus of rewards.
Representative simile: in this noble verse, their state in the extremity of their fright and terror – while they were being led to victory and booty – is likened to the state of one who is led to slaughter.

* Benefits:
3- The parsers' disagreement about «كما»: no one among the grammarians and exegetes remained who did not put in his bucket on its i'rab, and the views reached about fifteen. Were it not for the length, we would have set before you the sum of the grammarians' views and their implied forms. Although they almost come out of a single niche, what I feel to be sound is that the simile turns on two situations. The first: the believers' disagreement over the distribution of the spoils, so that ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said of it: «our conduct turned bad over it, so Allah took it out of our hands».
The second: their stance towards the Messenger's call to meet the army of Quraysh, and their inclination to meet the caravan (al-ʿīr) instead of the armed force (al-nafīr). So the kāf is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and the simile stands between two situations, both of which were heavy for the believers and which they disliked; as though He, Glorified is He, says: this situation is like the situation of such-and-such.. And if you are one of those with grammatical ambitions, turn to the lengthy works, for in them is what cools the breast and quenches the thirst.

safi-cedvel:58-58.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إمّا تخافنّ) like «إمّا تثقفنّ» «1»; (من قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «خيانة» — an adjective placed before what it qualifies —; (خيانة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (فانبذ إليهم) like «فشرّد بهم» «2», and the object of «انبذ» is omitted, i.e. the covenant; (على سواء) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) and the object together, i.e. "in a state of your being equal with them", or "in a state of their being equal with you" … in knowledge of the breaking of the covenant; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (لا) negating; (يحبّ) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is "huwa"; (الخائنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «تخافنّ …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «انبذ …» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يحبّ …» has no grammatical position, having the status of giving the reason (taʿlīl).
The clause «لا يحب الخائنين» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
[Translator's note: the markers «1» and «2» are in the source text without accompanying footnote text here.]

* Morphology:
(خيانة): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb خان يخون, of the bāb نصر; its pattern is فعالة with kasra on the fāʾ. There are other maṣdars: خون, with fatḥa on the khāʾ and sukūn on the wāw, and خانة … then a mīmī maṣdar, مخانة, with fatḥa on the mīm.

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit imaginative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-takhyīliyya): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً», fear is borrowed for knowledge, i.e. "If you come to know, of a people in covenant with you, a breaking of the covenant in what is to come, through the signs that appear to you from them, «فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ»".
2- The device of allusion (fann al-ishāra): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ». Some include it under the heading of concision (ījāz), since it branches off from it, but Qudāma made it a branch of the harmony of wording with meaning. Its explanation is that a small amount of wording indicates a great deal of meaning, so that the indication of the wording to the meaning is like pointing with the hand: with a single movement it points to many things which, if expressed by their names, would need a long expression and many words.
So the words of Allah the Exalted «فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ» point to the command to fight by casting off the covenant just as they cast off your covenant, together with the justice indicated by the command to act equally [Translator's note: the source reads «سال. مر بالمساواة», evidently garbled for «الأمر بالمساواة»]. If you add to that what the word «خيانة» points to, namely the existence of a previous treaty, it becomes clear to you what meanings these hidden allusions contain, as though they were a spell of magic.

* Benefits:
1- When is the covenant with the disbelievers broken?
This verse makes clear a legal ruling, namely the permissibility of annulling contracts of safe conduct with the disbelievers when we fear their treachery and betrayal, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did with Banū Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr when their treachery appeared. It is likewise obligatory to inform them of that annulment, so that no blame remains on the Muslims. But if they act treacherously and betray the covenant, informing them is not a condition, as happened with the disbelievers of Mecca when they broke the Truce of al-Ḥudaybiyya: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched on them without informing them.
A hadith has come on this matter: From Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir, from a man of Ḥimyar, who said: There was a covenant between Muʿāwiya and the Byzantines, and he was marching towards their lands to draw near, so that when the covenant expired he would raid them. Then a man came on a horse saying: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar! Fidelity, not treachery!" — and it was ʿAmr ibn ʿAnbasa. Muʿāwiya sent for him and asked him, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever has a covenant between himself and a people, let him not tighten a knot nor untie it until its term expires, or let him cast it back to them on equal terms." So Muʿāwiya went back. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī.
2- (The redundant) «ما»: In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted «وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ». We are concerned here with (إما), which is composed of the conditional «إن» and the redundant «ما». The grammarians said: in this case it is permissible to emphasise the verb or not to emphasise it, but the style of the Noble Quran has consistently emphasised it. The redundant «ما» occurs in many positions, of which we shall mention the most important:
1- After «إذا», as in the poet's words:
إذا ما الملك سام الناس خسفا ... أبينا أن نقر الذل فينا
(When a king inflicts humiliation on the people, we refuse to let abasement settle among us.)
2- After some prepositions, such as the bāʾ, as in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ».
And after «عن», as in the words of Allah the Exalted «عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نادِمِينَ».
3- It is added between the followed word and its follower, as in the words of Allah the Exalted «مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةً». Al-Zajjāj said: «ما» is a particle added for emphasis according to all the Basrans, and «بعوضة» is a badal (substitute).
4- It is added after «سيّ», as in the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ألا رب يوم لك منهن صالح ... ولا سيما يوم بدارة جلجل
(How many a good day you have had with them — and especially a day at Dārat Juljul.)

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) of prohibition, governing the jussive; (تحسبنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive, and (النون) is for emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent) [Note: Al-ʿUkbarī permitted making the fāʿil implied, i.e. (من خلفهم) "whoever is behind them" or (أحد) "anyone", so that the relative noun becomes the first mafʿūl bihi.], and the first object is omitted, its implied form being "themselves"; (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil; (سبقوا) like «كفروا»; (إنّ) a particle of emphasis governing the accusative, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (لا) negating; (يعجزون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …
and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «لا تحسبنّ الذين …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّهم لا يعجزون» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya) — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) —. The clause «لا يعجزون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكروا (remember); (يعد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (إحدى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الطائفتين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of anna; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّها لكم) is in the position of the accusative as badal (substitute) of the second object إحدى.. i.e. He promises you possession of one of the two parties. (الواو) conjunctive – or circumstantial (ḥāliyya) –; (تودّون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) like the first; (غير) ism of anna, accusative; (ذات) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الشوكة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (تكون) a complete imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «it» (هي), i.e. غير ذات الشوكة; (لكم) like the first, attached to (تكون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ غير ذات ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تودّون.
(الواو) conjunctive; (يريد) imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle of the accusative; (يحقّ) imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is «he»; (الحقّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحقّ) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يريد.
(بكلمات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحقّ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (يقطع دابر) like يحقّ الحقّ and conjoined to it; (الكافرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «(اذكروا) إذ يعدكم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعدكم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تودّون ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يعدكم [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (يعدكم).].
The clause «تكون لكم» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «يريد الله» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يحقّ الحقّ» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يقطع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يحقّ.
(اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يحقّ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil is «he», i.e. Allah; (الحقّ) like the first; (الواو) conjunctive; (يبطل الباطل) like يحقّ الحقّ and conjoined to it; (الواو) circumstantial; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (كره) past verb; (المجرمون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحقّ ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «He commanded you to fight» (أمركم بالقتال).
The clause «يحقّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يبطل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يحقّ ...
The clause «كره المجرمون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the object of the command, the linking pronoun being implied, i.e. even if the criminals dislike that.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the content of the preceding speech, i.e.: even if the criminals dislike the fighting, Allah has commanded you to it in order to establish the truth.

* Morphology:
(الشوكة): a noun meaning strength and might; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and it is borrowed from the singular of الشوك (thorns).

* Rhetoric:
The general and the specific (al-ʿumūm wa-l-khuṣūṣ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ الْباطِلَ» after His saying «يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ». The verification in distinguishing the two statements is that in the first the will is mentioned absolutely, not restricted to the particular event, as though it were said: you would like the unarmed party to be yours, while it is Allah the Exalted's way to will the establishing of the truth and the effacing of disbelief absolutely; and because of His will to establish the truth and abolish falsehood He assigned to you the armed party. So between the two statements there is generality and specificity, absoluteness and restriction. And in that there is evident intensification in emphasising the meaning by mentioning it in two ways: absolute and restricted.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) badal (substitute) of (إذ يعدكم), in the position of the accusative [Note: Or attached to the verb تودّون.], (تستغيثون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ربّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunctive; (استجاب) past verb, and the fāʿil is «he»; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استجاب), (أنّي) a particle resembling the verb and its ism; (ممدّ) khabar (predicate), nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بألف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the active participle ممدّ; (من الملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt (adjective) of ألف; (مردفين) ḥāl (circumstantial) of ألف, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي ممدّكم) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being بأنّي ممدّكم, attached to (استجاب).
The clause «تستغيثون ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «استجاب» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تستغيثون.

* Morphology:
(استجاب): the alif is changed from a wāw; its origin is استجوب. The wāw came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into «the fāʾ» [Translator's note: so in the source; «into an alif» is evidently meant.]; its pattern is استفعل [Note: The alif, sīn and tāʾ in the verb are extra without indicating anything, in contrast to تستغيثون, where they are extra for seeking.].
(ممدّكم): the active participle of the quadriliteral أمدّ; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn; the kasra of the ʿayn was moved to the letter before it because of the doubling.
(مردفين): plural of مردف, the active participle of the quadriliteral أردف; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- إذ: an adverb for past time. What can be drawn from its discussion has passed with us, so return to it in its places.
2- From history:
Muḥammad ﷺ called the Muslims to intercept the caravan of Quraysh returning from Syria. Abū Jahl learned of that, so he summoned Quraysh to protect it, and they set out for that. Abū Sufyān was at the head of the caravan; he veered with it onto the coastal road and escaped with it. Abū Jahl learned of that, but he was obstinate and refused anything but to reach the water of Badr, slaughter camels and drink wine.
When the setting-out of Quraysh reached Muḥammad, he consulted his Companions, both Muhājirūn and Anṣār, and opinion settled on meeting the army of the polytheists.
So Muḥammad ﷺ rejoiced and said: Go forth with the blessing of Allah, for Allah has promised me one of the two parties; by Allah, it is as if I am now looking at the places where the people will fall. Then came the battle of Badr, and Allah defeated the polytheists. The Muslims killed seventy of them and took seventy captive. The account of Badr is long; we have contented ourselves with this snippet of it.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* [Note: See the i'rab of this verse also in Sūrat (Āl ʿImrān), verse (126).]
I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) a negative particle; (جعل) past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (بشرى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the verb being transitive to one object.], the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunctive; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (تطمئنّ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تطمئنّ), (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تطمئنّ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «He prepared», «He did» or «He made easy» [Note: It may be conjoined to (بشرى) – as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi – and it was put in the genitive by the lām because a condition for the accusative was lacking.].
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative, inoperative (muhmala); (النصر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (إلّا) like the first; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) –; (الله) the Name of Majesty, ism of inna, accusative; (عزيز) khabar of inna, nominative; (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «جعله الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تطمئنّ به قلوبكم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أنّ) [Translator's note: so written in the source, with a shadda; the implied particle is أن.].
The clause «ما النصر إلا من عند الله» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله عزيز ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ يغشّيكم) like إذ يعدكم [Note: In verse (7) of this sūra.], and the fāʿil (agent) is «he», i.e. Allah; (النعاس) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (أمنة) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil [Note: Or of the first object, i.e. possessors of security, with a muḍāf omitted.. And it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).], (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أمنة; (الواو) conjunctive; (ينزّل) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is «he»; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينزّل), (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينزّل), (ماء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ليطهّر) like لتطمئنّ [Note: In the previous verse (1). [Translator's note: so in the source; the previous verse is (10).]], and the fāʿil is «he», and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (به) like منه, attached to (يطهّركم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يطهّركم) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (ينزّل).
(الواو) conjunctive; (يذهب) like يطهّر and conjoined to it; (عنكم) like عليكم, attached to (يذهب), (رجز) mafʿūl bihi; (الشيطان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (ليربط) like ليطهّر; (على قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يربط), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يربط) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يغشّيكم or ينزل).
(الواو) conjunctive; (يثبّت) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يربط), and the fāʿil is «he»; (به) like منه, attached to (يثبّت), (الأقدام) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «يغشّيكم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ينزّل ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يغشيكم.
The clause «يطهّركم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يذهب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative.
The clause «يربط ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يثبّت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يربط.

safi-cedvel:60-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (أعدّوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعدّوا); (ما) a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (استطعتم) past verb and its fāʿil; (من قوّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun; (الواو) conjunction; (من رباط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what «من قوّة» is attached to; (الخيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (ترهبون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (ترهبون); (عدوّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (عدوّكم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first, accusative … and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (آخرين) conjoined to the first «عدوّ», accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of «آخرين», and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negating; (تعلمون) like «ترهبون», and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (يعلم) imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) as before … and the second object of the verb is omitted, its implied form being "alarmed" or "at war"; but the apparent view is that the first verb is transitive to a single object, i.e. "you do not know them"; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a conditional noun governing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (تنفقوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من شيء) tamyīz (specification), accusative, or ḥāl, accusative [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. in the position of the accusative]; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (تنفقوا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (يوفّ) passive imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (إليكم) like «لهم», attached to (يوفّ); (الواو) of the ḥāl; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لا) negating; (تظلمون) passive imperfect verb, nominative … and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «أعدّوا لهم …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «استطعتم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما), the referent pronoun being omitted, its implied form being «استطعتموه».
The clause «ترهبون به …» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «أعدّوا» or from its object.
The clause «لا تعلمونهم» is in the position of the accusative as a second naʿt of «آخرين» [Note: Or a naʿt of «عدوّ», «عدوّكم» and «آخرين» together.].
The clause «الله يعلمهم» is in the position of the accusative as a third or further naʿt [Note: It is permissible for it to be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) with no grammatical position.].
The clause «يعلمهم» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «تنفقوا …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يوفّ إليكم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أنتم لا تظلمون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (إليكم).
The clause «لا تظلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
(الواو) conjunction; (إن) a conditional particle governing the jussive; (جنحوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (للسلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جنحوا); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition; (اجنح) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (لها) like «لهم», attached to (اجنح); (الواو) conjunction; (توكّل) like «اجنح»; (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (توكّل); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogating particle (nāsikh) —, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is «السميع», the nominal clause being the khabar of inna.]; (السميع) khabar of inna, nominative; (العليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «جنحوا …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «تنفقوا».
The clause «اجنح لها …» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «توكّل …» is in the position of the jussive, being conjoined to the apodosis of the condition.
The clause «إنّه هو السميع» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
(الواو) conjunction; (إن يريدوا) the conditional particle and the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يخدعوا) imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogating particle —; (حسب) the noun of inna, accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخدعوك) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
(هو) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as khabar; (أيّد) past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and (الكاف) as before; (بنصر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أيّد), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (بالمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the preceding preposition is attached to, for it is conjoined to it, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «يريدوا …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «جنحوا».
The clause «يخدعوك …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ حسبك الله» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هو الذي …» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption or giving the reason.
The clause «أيدك …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
(الواو) conjunction; (ألّف) like «أيّد»; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (ألّف); (قلوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (أنفقت) past verb and its fāʿil; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila of «ما»; (جميعا) ḥāl, accusative; (ما) particle of negation; (ألّفت) like «أنفقت»; (بين قلوبهم) like the first, attached to (ألّفت); (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle of istidrāk (rectification) governing the accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of lākinna, accusative; (ألّف) like «أيّد»; (بين) like the first, attached to (ألّف), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّه عزيز حكيم) like «إنّ الله قويّ شديد» [Note: In verse (52) of this sura.].
The clause «ألّف …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أيّدك».
The clause «أنفقت …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ما ألّفت …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لكنّ الله ألّف …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «ألّف …» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.
The clause «إنّه عزيز …» has no grammatical position, having the status of giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(رباط): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb ربط; it is not the maṣdar of the quadriliteral رابط, because here it means confinement (ḥabs) … Al-Zamakhsharī said: «الرباط» is a name for the horses that are tethered in the way of Allah; it may be that they are named by «الرباط» in the sense of «المرابطة» (garrisoning), and it may be the plural of ربيط in the sense of مربوط (tethered); and the maṣdar here is annexed to its object. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «الرباط» is a noun from رابط مرابطة, when one stays constantly at the enemy's frontier.
(يوفّ): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) suited to the jussive: the alif was dropped from it; its pattern is يقعّ. [Translator's note: so in the source; the dropped letter is the final yāʾ (يوفّى), and the pattern would be expected as يفعّ.]

* Rhetoric:
The non-metaphorical trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُمْ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ» …
i.e. prepare against them what weapons you can, because they give strength, self-confidence and the ability to fight. So strength here is caused by the weapons, and the relation here is that of being caused (musabbabiyya).

* Benefits:
Artistic imagery in the Noble Quran:
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted «وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَها وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ». «السلم» is peace-making, which is something abstract, but the Quranic expression embodies it as though it were something tangible, by using the verb (جنح). On the other hand, the verb «جنح», by its sound, its meaning and what it creates in the imagination, depicts the sense of inclining and leaning towards reconciliation and peace. Here depiction and embodiment reach their utmost, and the imagination follows the image of peace and the inclining towards it as though it were present before one. If we tried to replace the verb «جنح» with another verb synonymous with it or close to it in meaning, that image would disappear and the movement and life in it would die. Herein lies the magic and inimitability of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: the choice of the word, the verb or the particle has come in a place that is its own, which cannot be exchanged or altered, as though the word had been placed by a balance and sent down into its appointed place.

safi-cedvel:12-13.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) badal (substitute) of the first [Note: In verse (11) of this sūra; and it may be attached to (يثبّت).], (يوحي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى الملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يوحي), (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of anna; (مع) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of anna, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي معكم) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. بأنّي معكم ..., attached to (يوحي).
(الفاء) connecting an implied apodosis; (ثبّتوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil; (السين) a particle of the future; (ألقي) like يوحي, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «I» (أنا); (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألقي), (الذين) a relative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (كفروا) like آمنوا; (الرعب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) conjunctive; (اضربوا) like ثبّتوا; (فوق) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the verb اضربوا, and the object of اضربوا is omitted, its implied form being اضربوهم [Note: Some allowed (فوق) to be moved out of adverbial use and made an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); Abū Ḥayyān rejected that.], (الأعناق) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (اضربوا) like ثبّتوا; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of كلّ بنان; (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (بنان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «يوحيّ ربّك» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ثبّتوا ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the fighting begins, then make firm ...
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «سألقي» has no grammatical position: an explanation of His saying أنّي معكم ... or a parenthesis between two conjoined clauses.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اضربوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause ثبّتوا.
The clause «اضربوا (the second)» is conjoined to the clause اضربوا (the first).
(ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition of causation; (أن) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator – and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of anna; (شاقّوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (رسول) conjoined by the wāw to the Name of Majesty, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم شاقّوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.. i.e. that torment or punishment is because of their opposing Allah the Exalted and His Messenger. (الواو) resumptive; (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يشاقق) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), given a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «he», referring to من; (الله) the Name of Majesty, like the previous, and likewise (رسوله), (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition [Note: Or it is causal, for those who make the recompense omitted, the clause after it being a reason for this recompense, i.e.: whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, He will punish him, for Allah is severe in punishment.], (إن) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator –; (الله) the Name of Majesty, ism of inna, accusative; (شديد) khabar, nominative; (العقاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position: a reason for the content of the preceding torment.
The clause «شاقّوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «من يشاقق ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشاقق ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.] The clause «إن الله شديد ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الأعناق): plural of عنق, a noun for the well-known body part; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and ḍamma or sukūn on the ʿayn; it is masculine and feminine.
(بنان): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the fingertips or the fingers; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ; its singular is بنانة.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (al-majāz): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنانٍ», the speech is figurative in naming the whole by the name of the part. البنان is the finger; He expressed it by the part, which is the finger, and meant the whole, which is the hands and feet. So the relation is part-to-whole (juzʾiyya).

* Benefits:
- Among the characteristics of the Arabic language is making pronunciation easy; therefore the Arabs agreed on things that are all means to this end, among them «assimilation» (al-idghām), which is of three kinds:
a- Obligatory: when the two like letters are both vowelled, under conditions that may reach eleven, whose detail the method of this book does not allow, e.g. «مدّ», originally مدد, and ملّ and حبّ, etc.
b- Permissible: assimilation is permissible in three cases. (The first) if the verb is a past verb beginning with two tāʾs, like تتبّع and تتابع: assimilation is permissible in both, and pronouncing it is made possible by adding the connecting hamza, so one says اتّبع and اتّابع. (The second and third) that the word is a jussive imperfect verb, or an imperative verb indeclinable on the sukūn; in it both separation and assimilation are permissible, like the verb يشاقق in the verse referred to.
b- [Translator's note: so lettered in the source; «c» is meant.] Assimilation is prohibited if one of the two like letters, the first or the second, is vowelled [Translator's note: so in the source.], or if the first is a hāʾ of pause, or a long vowel at the end, or a separated hamza.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلكم) like the preceding [Note: In the previous verse (13).], and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being «occurring» (واقع) or «deserved» (مستحقّ) [Note: (ذلك) may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «the matter» or «the punishment».], (الفاء) conjunctive [Note: According to Abū Ḥayyān, it is the answer of an implied command, i.e. take heed, then taste it.], (ذوقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunctive; (أنّ) like the previous [Note: In the previous verse (13).]. (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar of أنّ; (عذاب) the postponed ism of anna, accusative (manṣūb); (النار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «ذلكم (واقع)» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ذو قوه» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. take heed, then taste it..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ للكافرين عذاب ...) is in the position of the nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «the decreed thing» or «the necessary thing».. or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being «decreed», i.e. the fixedness of the torment of the Fire for the disbelievers is decreed [Note: It may be in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being اعلموا (know).].
The clause of the interpreted maṣdar – the mubtadaʾ and khabar – has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
The shift (al-iltifāt): in the noble verse, since the address in it is to the disbelievers by way of a shift from the third person.

* Benefits:
1- «ذلكم»:
It is known to all grammarians that «ذا» is a demonstrative, that the lām is for distance, and that the kāf is a particle of address. What we want to clarify is that the demonstrative «ذلك» is always followed by a particle suited to the one addressed in singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine. So you say: ذلك for the singular, ذلكما for the dual, ذلكم for the masculine plural and ذلكنّ for the feminine plural. In the discussion of the demonstrative there is detail and clarification that we have passed over, in keeping with our method in this book.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative, and (ها) for alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as badal (substitute) of أيّ or its naʿt (adjective) [Translator's note: so in the source, «in the position of the accusative».]; (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إذا) a conditional adverb for the future, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (لقيتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (الذين) a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كفروا) like آمنوا; (زحفا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of the ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (لقيتم), or of the subject pronoun, or of both together [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted ḥāl, i.e. زاحفين زحفا (advancing in an advance).], (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-making; (تولّوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (الأدبار) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb).
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لقيتم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تولّوهم ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
(الواو) conjunctive; (من يولّ) like من يشاقق, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يولّ) [Note: It may be indeclinable because it is annexed to an indeclinable adverb, namely (إذ).], (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi [Note: The nunation here is the nunation of compensation (tanwīn ʿiwaḍ), compensating for an omitted clause, i.e. يوم إذ لقيتموهم (on the day when you meet them).], (دبر) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (متحرّفا) accusative as excepted from an implied general ḥāl [Note: I.e. whoever turns his back to them in whatever state, except turning aside ... If that is not implied, the entry of (إلّا) is not valid, because the condition is affirmative, not negated.. Some make (متحرّفا) excepted from those who turn their backs, i.e. whoever turns his back to them.. except a man turning aside; al-Zamakhsharī said this.], (لقتال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the active participle متحرّف; (أو) a conjunction; (متحيّزا) conjoined to (متحرّفا), accusative; (إلى فئة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (متحيّزا), (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (باء) past verb, and the fāʿil is «he»; (بغضب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil, i.e. clothed with or accompanied by wrath; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of غضب; (الواو) conjunctive; (مأوى) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جهنّم) khabar (predicate), nominative, (الواو) conjunctive; (بئس) an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for the performative of blame; (المصير) fāʿil, nominative.. and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being جهنّم.
The clause «من يولّهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «يولّهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «قد باء بغضب» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «مأواه جهنّم» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «بئس المصير» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(زحفا): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb زحف; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(تولّوا): it contains a weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion. Its origin is تولّيوا with ḍamma on the yāʾ; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so its vowel was moved to the letter before it; when two sukūns met, the yāʾ, the final radical of the word, was deleted and it became تولّوا; its pattern is تفعّوا.
(يولّهم): it contains a weakening by deletion in keeping with the jussive; its origin is يولّيهم; its pattern is يفعّهم.
(متحرّفا): the active participle of the five-letter تحرّف, so its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(متحيّزا): the active participle of the five-letter تحيّز, so its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. It contains a weakening, because its origin is متحيوز: the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ.
(باء): it contains a weakening by change, since the alif is originally a wāw – its imperfect is يبوء – and its origin is بوأ. The wāw came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into «the fāʾ» [Translator's note: so in the source; «into an alif» is evidently meant.].

* Rhetoric:
The figure of allusion (fann al-taʿrīḍ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَمَنْ يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ». He mentioned to them a state that is deemed shameful in the one who does it, so He used the word الدبر (the rear) rather than الظهر (the back). Some include it within metonymy (al-kināya).
al-Saʿd al-Taftāzānī said: «When the metonymy is incidental, brought for the sake of a qualified thing that is not mentioned, it is fitting to call it allusion (al-taʿrīḍ). One says عرضت لفلان and عرضت بفلان when you say something while meaning him, as though you pointed to one side while intending another side; and from it are the indirect expressions (al-maʿārīḍ) in speech, which is the concealment (al-tawriya) of a thing by another thing.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ}: There are three views on it, the clearest of which is that it is an adverbial (ẓarf) whose governing verb is omitted, its implied form being: "and remember your condition, firmly established at the time of your fewness." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The second is that it is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is accusative as an explicitly mentioned direct object, not as an adverbial; that is: remember the time of your being few and abased." There is room for objection in this, because «إذ» is not used freely (as a noun) except in the ways I mentioned earlier, and this is not one of them. The third is that it is an adverbial of «اذكروا». Al-Ḥūfī said this, and it is invalid, because the governing word is future while the adverbial is past, so how could the two meet?
His saying: {تَخَافُونَ}: There are three views on it, the most apparent being that it is a third khabar (predicate). The second is that it is an adjective (ṣifa) of «قليل»; the description has begun with the singular and then moved to the sentence. The third is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in «مُسْتَضْعَفُون».

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وتخونوا}: It may be accusative by an implied «أَنْ» as the answer to a prohibition, that is: "do not combine the two offences," as in his saying:
2404 - لا تَنْهَ عن خُلُقٍ وتأتيَ مثلَه ... عارٌ عليك إذا فَعَلْت عظيمُ
(Do not forbid a trait while doing the like of it; it is a great disgrace on you when you do.)
The second is that it is jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the first. This second view is preferable, because it contains a prohibition of each one separately, unlike the first, which is a prohibition of combining the two; and a prohibition of combining two things does not necessarily entail a prohibition of each one separately. The treatment of this has already been given at {وَتَكْتُمُواْ الحق} [al-Baqara: 42], at the beginning of al-Baqara.
«أماناتِكم» is on the omission of a muḍāf, that is: "those entrusted with your trusts" (aṣḥāba amānātikum). It is also possible that they were forbidden to betray the trusts themselves, by way of exaggeration, as though the trusts had been made things that are betrayed. Mujāhid read «أمانتكم» in the singular, and it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr, the plural being meant.
«وأنتم تعلمون» is a ḥāl clause. The object of the knowing may be intended, that is: "you know the ugliness of that," or "that you will be held to account for it." It is also possible not to supply one, that is: "you are among those possessed of knowledge." The knowing may be taken in its ordinary sense, or in the sense of recognition (ʿirfān).

semin-durr:29-29.t:
The discussion of «الفرقان» has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara. What is meant by it here is that which brings one out of error, or the thing that separates truth from falsehood. Mazrad ibn Ḍirār said:
2405 - بادَرَ الأفقَ أن يغيبَ فلمَّا ... أظلم الليلُ لم يَجِدْ فُرْقانا
(He hastened to the horizon before it should vanish; but when the night grew dark he found no deliverance [furqān].)
Another said:
2406 - ما لك مِنْ طولِ الأَسى فُرْقانُ ... بعد قَطينٍ رحلوا وبانُوا
(You have no relief [furqān] from long grief after the household that departed and went away.)
Another said:
2407 - وكيف أُرَجِّي الخلدَ والموتُ طالبي ... وما ليَ من كأسِ المنية فرقانُ
(How can I hope for immortality while death is seeking me, and I have no escape [furqān] from the cup of death?)

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ}: This adverbial is conjoined to the adverbial before it, and «ليُثْبتوك» is attached to «يَمْكُرُ». "Fixing" (tathbīt) here means striking until the one struck has no movement left. He said:
2408 - فقلت وَيْحَكَ ماذا في صحيفتكمْ ... قالوا الخليفةُ أمسى مُثْبَتاً وجِعا
(I said, "Woe to you, what is in your letter?" They said, "The caliph has become laid low, in pain.")
Ibn Wathāb read «لِيُثَبِّتوك», making the verb transitive by doubling the middle radical. Al-Nakhaʿī read «ليُبَيِّتُوك», from bayāt (night attack).

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هُوَ الحق}: The majority read «الحق» in the accusative; it is the khabar of "to be" (kawn) and «هو» is a separator pronoun (faṣl), which has already been treated at length. Al-Akhfash said «هو» is redundant (zāʾid), meaning what was said before, that it is a faṣl. Al-Aʿmash and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «الحق» in the nominative; the explanation is clear: «هو» is nominative as mubtadaʾ and «الحق» is its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of "to be," as in his saying:
2409 - ... تَحِنُّ إلى ليلى وأنت تركتَها
وكنتَ عليها بالمَلا أنت أقدرُ
(... You long for Laylā though you left her, and you were more able [to keep] her in the open country.)
This is the dialect of Tamīm. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "In Arabic it is permissible to put «الحق» in the nominative as the khabar of «هو», the sentence being the khabar of «كان»." Al-Zajjāj said: "I do not know anyone who read with this permissible form." I say: it has become clear who read it so, and they are two eminent men.
His saying: {مِنْ عِندِكَ} is a ḥāl from the meaning of «الحق», that is: "the established, in the state of its being from You." His saying {مِّنَ السمآء} has two views. One is that it is attached to the verb before it. The second is that it is an adjective of «حجارة», so it is attached to an omitted word. As for their saying «من السماء» although rain comes only from it, al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is as if he wanted it to be said, 'then rain down upon us sijjīl,' and he put «حجارة من السماء» in its place, as one says 'he poured over him a masrūda of iron,' meaning 'a coat of mail.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "He means by that emphasis," and said: "just as the meaning of «من حديد» is emphasis, because a masrūd (riveted) thing is only of iron, as rain is only from the sky." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Their saying «من السماء» is exaggeration and hyperbole." The Shaykh said: "What appears is that the wisdom in their saying «من السماء» is that they were matching the coming of the rain from the direction from which he, peace be upon him, had said revelation comes to him; that is: 'You claim that revelation comes to you from the sky, so bring us punishment from the direction from which revelation comes to you.' They said it in order to deem it far-fetched."

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ}: The discussion of this lām, called lām al-juḥūd (the lām of denial), has already been given. The majority read it with kasra. Abū l-Sammāl read it with fatḥa. Ibn ʿAṭiyya reported from Abū Zayd: "I heard some of the Arabs say «لَيعذبهم» with fatḥa on the lām; it is an unfamiliar dialect, not used in the Qur'an." I say: he means in the well-known reading, and he did not count the reading of Abū l-Sammāl. Ibn Mujāhid reported from Abū Zayd the fatḥa of every lām from some Arabs, except in «الحمد لله». ʿAbd al-Wārith reported from Abū ʿAmr the fatḥa of the lām of command in {فَلْيَنظُرِ الإنسان إلى طَعَامِهِ} [ʿAbasa: 24].
He brought the khabar of the first «كان» differently from how he brought it in the second. It is either omitted, namely "intending" (irāda), as the Basrans supply it, that is: "Allah was not intending to punish them" — and the negation of the intention of punishment is more emphatic than the negation of punishment — or else he emphasised it with the lām, in the view of the Kufans, because his being among them is a stronger reason than their seeking forgiveness; for the difference is great between his, peace be upon him, presence among them and their seeking forgiveness.
His saying: {وَأَنتَ فِيهِمْ} is a ḥāl, and likewise {وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ}. The apparent view is that all the pronouns refer to the disbelievers. It was also said that the pronoun in «يُعَذِّبهم» and «مُعَذِّبهم» refers to the disbelievers, while the pronoun in «وهم» refers to the believers. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وهم يستغفرون» is in the position of ḥāl, and its meaning is the negation of seeking forgiveness from them; that is: if they were of those who believe and seek forgiveness for disbelief, He would not have punished them, as in the saying of the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ القرى بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ} [Hūd: 114]; but they do not seek forgiveness and do not believe, and that is not expected of them." This meaning that he mentioned is transmitted from Qatāda and Abū Zayd, and Ibn Jarīr preferred it.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أن لا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ}: There are two views on «أن». The first, which is the apparent one, is that it is a maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya), and its position is either accusative or genitive, because it is on the omission of the preposition; the implied form is: "in that He not punish them." This preposition and its genitive noun are attached to what «لهم» is attached to, namely being established; the implied meaning is: "what has been established for them concerning Allah's not punishing them," meaning that they have no share in the absence of punishment. The second is that it is redundant (zāʾida), which is the view of al-Akhfash. Al-Naḥḥās said: "If it were as he said, it would have made «يُعَذِّبهم» nominative." That is, the verb should have been nominative as standing in the position of ḥāl, as in {وَمَا لَنَا لاَ نُؤْمِنُ بالله} [al-Māʾida: 84]. But redundancy does not entail absence of effect; do you not see that «مِنْ» and the bāʾ operate although they are added? Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It was also said that it is a ḥāl, but that is remote, because «أَنْ» makes the verb exclusively future." The apparent view is that «ما» in «وما لهم» is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) and is an interrogative with the meaning of affirmation, that is: "How should they not be punished while they are characterised by this state?" It was also said that «ما» is negative, so it is a statement of that, that is: it is not the case that there is no punishment, i.e. punishment is not removed from them while they are engaged in this state.
His saying: {وَمَا كانوا أَوْلِيَآءَهُ}: There are two views on this sentence. One is that it is resumptive, and the hāʾ refers to the mosque, that is: "they were not the guardians of the mosque." The second is that it is conjoined to the preceding ḥāl clause, which is «وهم يَصُدُّون», and the meaning is: how should Allah not punish them while they are characterised by these two attributes: their barring from the Sacred Mosque and their not being its guardians? It is also possible that the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, that is: "they were not Allah's guardians."
[Translator's note: the source text has «هذبن» in «هذبن الوَصْفَيْن», evidently a misprint for «هذين»; translated as "these two".]

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ مُكَآءً وَتَصْدِيَةً}: That is: nothing of what they count as prayer and worship was anything but these two acts, namely mukāʾ and taṣdiya; that is, if they had a prayer, it was nothing but these two, as in the poet's saying:
2410 - وما كنت أخشى أن يكونَ عطاؤُه ... أداهِمَ سُوداً أو مُحَدْرَجَةً سُمْرا
(I never feared that his gift would be black fetters or tightly twisted brown whips.)
He put the fetters and the whips in the place of the gift.
Al-mukāʾ is the maṣdar of makā yamkū, that is: he whistled between his fingers or between his palms. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "I said to Musajjiʿ ibn Nabhān: 'What is meant by "his farīṣa makes a mukāʾ sound"?' So he interlaced his fingers, put them to his mouth and blew into them." I say: he means the saying of ʿAntara:
2411 - وحَليلِ غانيةٍ تركتُ مُجَدَّلاً ... تَمْكُو فريصتُه كشِدْق الأَعْلَمِ
(Many a husband of a fair woman I left sprawled, his farīṣa whistling like the split lip of a hare-lipped man.)
It is said: makat al-farīṣa, that is: it made a sound with the blood. And makat ist al-dābba, that is: it blew out wind. Mujāhid said: al-mukkāʾ is a whistling in the tune of a white bird found in the Hijaz. The poet said:
2412 - إذا غرَّد المُكَّاء في غير روضةٍ ... فويلٌ لأهل الشَّاءِ والحُمُرات
(When the mukkāʾ warbles in a place that is not a meadow, then woe to the owners of sheep and donkeys.)
Al-mukkāʾ is of the form fuʿʿāl, a pattern of intensity. Abū ʿUbayda said: "One says makā yamkū mukūwan and mukāʾan: he whistled. Al-mukāʾ with ḍamma is like al-bukāʾ and al-ṣurākh." It was said that of the names of sounds only al-ghināʾ and al-nidāʾ depart from this by taking kasra.
As for al-taṣdiya, there are two views on it. The first is that it is from al-ṣadā, which is the echo of a voice heard in empty hard places. From it one says ṣadiya yaṣdā taṣdiya, and what is meant by it here is the sound of clapping, of one hand against the other. In the exegesis: when the polytheists heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying and reciting the Qur'an, they clapped their hands and whistled with their mouths, to distract those who were listening to him and to confuse his recitation. This fits his saying: {لاَ تَسْمَعُواْ لهذا القرآن والغوا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 26]. It was also said that it is derived from taṣdida, which is uproar, shouting and clapping, and that one of the two dāls was replaced by yāʾ for lightness. What indicates this is his saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا قَوْمُكَ مِنْهُ يَصِدُّونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 57] in the reading of those who read the ṣād with kasra, that is: they raise an uproar and clamour. This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. Abū Jaʿfar al-Rustumī rejected it and said: "It is only from al-ṣadā, so how can it be made from a geminated root?" Abū ʿAlī rejected Abū Jaʿfar's rejection and said: "It is established that yaṣuddūn is of the kind of sound, so its derivation is from that, and taṣdiya is of the form tafʿila," and then he said much more. The second view is that it is from al-ṣadd, which is prevention, the original being taṣdida with two dāls too, the second of which was replaced by yāʾ. What supports this is the reading of those who read «يَصُدُّون» with ḍamma, that is: they prevent.
The majority read «صلاتُهم» in the nominative and «مُكاءً» in the accusative. Abān ibn Taghlib, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim, with a difference reported from them, read «وما كان صلاتَهم» with «صلاتَهم» accusative and «مكاءٌ» nominative. Al-Fārisī judged this reading wrong and said: "It is not permissible to predicate a definite noun of an indefinite one except out of necessity, as in the saying of Ḥassān:
2413 - كأنَّ سَبيئةً مِنْ بيت رَأْسٍ ... يكونُ مزاجَها عَسَلٌ وماءُ
(As if wine from Bayt Raʾs, its mixture being honey and water.)"
Abū l-Fatḥ explained it on the basis that al-mukāʾ and al-taṣdiya are generic nouns (ism jins), meaning that they are two maṣdars. He said: "In a generic noun the definite and the indefinite are close to each other, so why should it be said that one of the two is made the subject and the other the predicate?" This is close to the noun defined by generic «أل» when it is described by a sentence, as an indefinite is described by it, as in his saying, the Exalted: {وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ الليل نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ النهار} [Yā Sīn: 37], and the saying of the other:
2414 - ولقد مَرَرْتُ على اللئيم يَسُبُّني ... فَمَضَيْتُ ثُمَّتَ قلتُ لا يَعْنيني
(I passed by the base man as he was abusing me; I went on, then said, "He does not mean me.")
Some of them said: "Abū ʿAmr read «إلا مُكاً» with the short form and tanwīn; this is as they said bukāʾ and bukā, with long and short vowel." The poet combined the two forms:
2415 - بَكَتْ عيني وحُقَّ لها بُكاها ... وما يُغْني البكاءُ ولا العويلُ
(My eye wept, and it has the right to its weeping; but neither weeping nor wailing avails.)
[Translator's note: in the source the quotation of "some of them said" is opened but never closed, and this entry ends there.]

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِيَمِيزَ الله الخبيث}: The disagreement about it has already been given in Āl ʿImrān. His saying «ويَجْعل»: it may be taken as meaning "to make into" (taṣyīr), governing two objects, or as meaning "to cast," governing one. On either reading «بعضه» is a badal baʿḍ min kull (partial substitute), and on the first view «على بعض» is in the position of the second object, while on the second it is attached to the act of placing itself, as in your saying "you placed your goods, some of them upon others." Abū l-Baqāʾ, after ruling that it takes one object, said: "It was also said that the preposition and its genitive noun is a ḥāl, the implied form being: 'and He places the vile one, some of it high above some.'"
The lām in «ليميز» is attached to «يُحشرون». One says mayyaztuhu fa-tamayyaza and miztuhu fa-immāza. It was also read anomalously {وانمازوا اليوم} [Yā Sīn: 59]. Abū Zayd recited:
2416 - لمَّا نبا اللهُ عني شرَّ غَدْرتِه ... وانْمِزْتُ لا مُنْسِئاً غَدْراً ولا وَجِلا
(When Allah turned away from me the evil of his treachery, and I separated myself, neither postponing treachery nor fearful.)
The difference between these words has already been given in Āl ʿImrān.
His saying: {فَيَرْكُمَهُ} is conjoined to the accusative before it. Al-rakm is your gathering one thing upon another until it becomes a heap (rukām) and heaped up (markūm), as sand and cloud are heaped; from it {يَقُولُواْ سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ} [al-Ṭūr: 44]. Al-murtakam is the main road, because of the heaping (rakm) in it, that is: the crowding of the passers-by and their tracks. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl. According to some it may be tawkīd (emphasis).

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِلَّذِينَ كفروا}: There are the two well-known views on this lām. The first is that it is for conveying (tablīgh): he was commanded to convey to them the meaning of this sentence quoted after "say," whether he gave it in this wording or in another wording conveying its meaning. The second is that it is causal (taʿlīl), which is what al-Zamakhsharī said, and he denied that it is for conveying, saying: "That is: say this saying on their account: if they desist. Had it meant that he should address them with it, it would have been said: 'If you desist, He will forgive you,' which is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd. Similar to it is {وَقَالَ الذين كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ} [al-Aḥqāf: 11]: they addressed it to others, [on their account,] so that they might hear it."
